description: v1.6.27 (MICRO le entità spaziotemporali, decided by E.D. 2026-10-10): DocumentNode and AuthorNode (with AuthorAINode) are SPATIOTEMPORAL ENTITIES like the stratigraphic units — the top-level block `spatiotemporal_entities` names the three classes and what they share: a start and an end (absolute_time_start / absolute_time_end, read with the label of their owner: a person is born and dies, a model is released and retired), the lane of the matrix where they begin (has_first_epoch) and the ones they last through (survive_in_epoch), their place in the sequence (is_after, has_same_time), an activity. The edges are widened in connections 1.6.38; the chronology dates the three with the same rules (Graph.CHRONOLOGY_TYPES). AuthorNode and DocumentNode gain a `spatiotemporal` element saying how their time reads; no field of theirs changes. v1.6.26 (H4, decided by E.D. 5 Oct 2026, «Heriverse legge l'em.json e sceglie la versione»): ResourceNode.use admits two more uses, heriverse and aton — a version made FOR a viewer, the package on disk that Heriverse or another ATON app opens offline (EM Tools makes it with «Prepare for a use…», as is: no optimisation of its own); a viewer asks heriverse, aton, web, realtime in that order (s3dgraphy.resources.versions.choose_version). v1.6.25 (D1, MICRO un solo vocabolario, decided by E.D. 4 Oct 2026): GeoPositionNode.rotation_reference = 'grid' (D2: the rotation is measured from the GRID north of the CRS). ResourceNode.lod_level (em:lodLevel, computed from the chain, written only on export and checked at load), ResourceNode.use (em:use, a list of analysis | realtime | web | mobile_ar | print | render | preview) and seven measures of a version (em:trisPerM2, em:texelDensityDD, em:textureCount, em:textureSidePx, em:uvRatio, em:reductionFromLod0, em:geometricErrorM). v1.6.24 (dev30, decided by E.D. 2026-10-02 on the dev29 report): DTCAcquisitionNode.retrieved_from — where a retrieved object came from, a DOI or a URL (em:retrievedFrom, D1; optional, validate warns «download without origin»). ResourceNode.members_digest names em:membersDigest, the digest of a file_set with a predicate of its own beside em:checksum + em:digestCovers (D4; not a second field). ResourceNode.packaging carries its vocabulary with values and labels, translated in datamodel_translations.json (packagings; A3). ResourceNode.content_digest also holds the digest of the data of a master inside another file — a Metashape model's mesh.ply — compared, never verified by downloading (D7). GCPSetNode gains data.control (ground_control_points | camera_positions) and data.accuracy_m: a chunk referenced only by its cameras' GPS is absolute with the control said for what it is, and validate warns «georeferenced only by camera GPS» (D7). Node.properties.lang states the one explicit exception to the AI marker: a recognised language confirmed by a person is data.lang only (U5). CRMem 1.6.14. v1.6.23 (dev29, 2026-10-02, measured on San Pietro): seven properties that the round trip em.json → TTL → em.json lost now leave and come back — ResourceNode packaging / tier / digest_covers / content_digest (em:packaging, em:tier, em:digestCovers, em:contentDigest) and the declared fields of a DTC step, technique / parameters / software (em:technique, em:parameters, em:software, the last two as rdf:JSON). digest_covers admits members (a file_set). The blend:// locator stays out of RDF on purpose: it is a private path. v1.6.22 (dev28, 2026-11-01, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01 on the dev27 report): the access mode of a signature (created_auth / modified_auth / validated_auth) admits a third mode, 'declared' — an iD typed in a tool's preferences and checked by nobody (EMStudio's declared identity, EM Tools' local identity), with no attested_by; through a relay the mode is the relay's, read from the token (crdt.stamp_auth), not the client's declaration. The language a node is born in travels in the add_node op (crdt.make_op requires it of the producer, 'und' when unknown); the study's language is read only for old ops, said and counted. CRMem 1.6.12. v1.6.21 (dev27, 2026-10-31, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01, «il testo, la risorsa e la selezione» and «l'accesso sul campo»): ResourceNode.properties gains lang — on a resource the language(s) of its CONTENT, one tag or a sorted list, leaving as dcterms:language and outside the cascade of the texts — addresses (several addresses of ONE resource, same digest: em:hasAddress with em:locator, em:residency, em:checkedAt, em:reachable) and checksum_at (a dated digest, em:checksumAt). Node.properties gains created_auth / modified_auth / validated_auth: how the hand of a signature had entered, {mode: orcid | node_password, attested_by} (em:createdVia / em:modifiedVia / em:validatedVia, em:authMode, em:attestedBy). data.lang is written at birth (s3dgraphy.language.stamp_birth_language), also when equal to the study's. v1.6.20 (MICRO le traduzioni, 2026-10-29, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01, «Le traduzioni»): NEW TranslationNode (TRANSL, crm:E33_Linguistic_Object) — ONE translation of one text field of one node. The original stays a string in its field (data.lang on the node, else the study's), never overwritten; each translation is a node reached by has_translation (crm:P73_has_translation, connections 1.6.34) with data.lang (arrival), data.from_lang (departure, written because the original can change), data.field (CRDT vocabulary: description | data.<key>; a PropertyNode's value is data.value; never name), data.text, data.method (manual | ai | edition), data.source_digest (sha256 of the original translated: a different digest = «da riallineare») and data.review_requested («da rivedere»). Who: has_author; AI: data.ai_assisted, unverified until validated_by; an edition: extracted_from → the DocumentNode. RDF (em.ttl 1.6.10): Node.properties.lang names em:originalLanguage — the node's own data.lang leaves as that literal whenever it is declared, equal to the study's too, so a reader tells the original literal from the translations that share its predicate and the round trip gives data.lang back exactly where it was (the D.1 limit of 1.6.19 is closed); the TranslationNode's fields name em:sourceLanguage, em:translatedField, em:translationMethod, em:sourceDigest, em:reviewRequested. v1.6.19 (MICRO la lingua dei dati, 2026-10-27, decided by E.D. 2026-09-28): Node.properties.description becomes an object {cidoc: P3_has_note, natural_language: true, note} — the MARKER that says the description is text in a natural language and leaves in RDF with its language tag; declared once on the base class and inherited by every node type. name is NOT marked: names are invariant identities. No field added, no node element, no graph change: the em.json is the same; only the RDF literal gains its tag. v1.6.18 (MICRO i termini di em.ttl nel datamodel, 2026-10-26, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01 — the datamodel JSON is the truth, so every em: term of em.ttl is cited by a datamodel or is a written exception): the em: predicates the RDF exporter already writes are now NAMED in properties, as plain-string mapping notes (no field added, no node element, no graph change). Node (inherited by every class): the last-hand stamps created_by em:createdBy / modified_by em:lastEditedBy / modified_at em:modifiedAt (created_at prov:generatedAtTime), the tombstone removed.ts em:removedAt / removed.by em:removedBy, the AI marker ai_assisted.by em:aiAssistedBy / .model em:aiModel / .prompt_ref em:aiPromptRef / .fields em:aiAssistedField and the verification validated_by em:validatedBy / validated_at em:validatedAt (properties_note). ResourceNode: checksum em:checksum, scope em:resourceScope, residency em:residency. SemanticShapeNode: convexshapes em:convexShape, spheres em:sphere. AnnotationRegionNode: crs em:crs, coords.frame_iri em:LocalSceneFrame. AuthorNode and AuthorAINode: verified em:orcidVerified (AuthorAINode also names orcid P48, which the exporter writes for both). LocationNodeGroup.propagation.mapping: uri em:propagation. THREE ENTRIES CORRECTED TO WHAT THE CODE WRITES (measured in rdf_exporter.py): PropertyNode.property_type was P2_has_type, is em:hasQualiaType; AuthorAINode model / prompt_reference were P3_has_note, are em:modelIdentifier / em:promptReference; ResourceFileNode.checksum was P1_is_identified_by, is em:checksum; and LocationNodeGroup.propagation said 'not serialized to triplestore' while the exporter has written the non-default value as em:propagation since c1a702c (2026-08-12). v1.6.17 (MICRO la risorsa e i suoi file, 2026-10-18, decided by E.D. 2026-09-30): NEW ResourceFileNode (FILE, crmdig:D1_Digital_Object) — the ResourceNode is the set, the ResourceFileNode is each file, reached by has_file (connections 1.6.30) with role and relative path on the edge. With one file the node is implicit (url and checksum stay on the ResourceNode, as today). ResourceNode.PACKAGINGS += file_set (a few files that call each other: obj → mtl → textures, gltf → bin, shp and companions) and datablock (one object inside a file, a blend:// locator). Representations of the same thing are sibling ResourceNodes tied by dtc_derived_from and chosen by tier and packaging. ADDITIVE: nothing narrowed, no graph changes. v1.6.16 (MICRO le annotazioni ATON sull'asset, 2026-10-15, decided by E.D.): AnnotationRegionNode gains geometry_kind 'volume' — an annotation that encloses a part of a 3D model (ATON / Hathor convex hulls and spheres) and is the proxy of no unit. The region carries no vertices: it reaches a SemanticShapeNode (convexshapes, spheres) with has_semantic_shape and the model with is_on_resource. geometry.aton.import_aton_scene makes one for every semantic id no EM node is named after (a stratigraphic unit only with an explicit create_type); api.promote_region_to_proxy turns it into the proxy of a unit later. RDF: P2_has_type 'volume', no selector, no WKT; the shape travels as itself. Additive. v1.6.15 (MICRO la geometria per origine, 2026-10-11, decided by E.D. 2026-09-30): AnnotationRegionNode's point / line / polyline keep their vertices IN THE NODE, data.coords [[x, y, z], ...] (scene-local, glTF Y-up, metres) with crs and, for a line or a polyline, length and unit — no .glb and no SemanticShape for a reading. New block coords (inline_max_vertices 500: above it the vertices go to a .glb resource via has_linked_resource, with a warning). RDF: geo:hasGeometry -> <region>/geometry geo:asWKT (POINT Z / LINESTRING Z, GeoSPARQL). The readings/<id>.glb of 2026-10-06 are migrated on opening. v1.6.14 (MICRO la cattura in RDF, 2026-09-30): DTCAcquisitionNode.mapping.by_kind — its D12 is the class of a retrieval; a capture takes the class its kind declares in em_visual_rules 1.6.24 (D2 / D11 / E65). Mapping text only, no field changed. v1.6.13 (MICRO i generi delle US, 2026-09-30, decided by E.D. the same day): stratigraphic_kind gains 'coating' — the USR (rivestimento) and its English translation USS (surface): plaster, floors, revetments — with `labels`, `codes` and `default_code` per kind; new node element `source_code` (data.source_code) keeps the code a unit came in with when it is not its kind's default, so the way back to pyArchInit gives the same code. A legacy node_type 'USR' / 'USS' opens as US + coating. v1.6.12 (MICRO la cattura nel DTC e le murature, 2026-09-30): StratigraphicUnit (US) gains the node element `stratigraphic_kind` (em.json data.stratigraphic_kind; today one value, 'masonry'): a USM is a US + masonry, and the legacy node_type 'USM' — never a type of this datamodel — opens as that. DTCAcquisitionNode's description names the two families of the acquisition axis (em_visual_rules 1.6.22: capture / retrieval). v1.6.11 (MICRO la misura in RDF, 2026-10-07): AnnotationRegionNode.properties says how the fields left unprojected by 1.6.10 now travel — the quote of a passage as oa:TextQuoteSelector, the length of a line/polyline as crm:E54_Dimension (P90 value, P91 QUDT unit, em:crs), vertex_count as em:vertexCount. CRMem (em.ttl) 1.6.5 -> 1.6.6. Mapping text only, no field changed. v1.6.10 (MICRO la geometria della lettura, 2026-10-06, decided by E.D. on 2026-09-29): AnnotationRegionNode becomes the node of THE PLACE A READING LOOKED AT, with a new field geometry_kind: region2d (default, every older region), passage (start, end, text), point, line, polyline. The three 3D kinds keep their coordinates in a .glb (glTF POINTS / LINES / LINE_STRIP) linked with has_semantic_shape exactly like a proxy's payload, never in the em.json; the node keeps vertex_count and, for line/polyline, length + unit + crs (api.measure). See the entry's geometry_kinds and glb_payload. Paired with connections 1.6.27 (is_on_resource.target += the representation models). Additive: a region without geometry_kind reads as region2d. v1.6.9 (MICRO la definizione dell'unita', 2026-10-20, decided by E.D. on 2026-09-27): StratigraphicNode.properties gains `definition`, the DEFINIZIONE of the US sheet, as an element of the node like name and description and NOT a qualia. Value = a controlled-vocabulary concept {concept, label}; em.json carries it as data.definition (CRDT field 'data.definition', no change to the frozen em.json v1 node shape); inherited by every stratigraphic subtype. The RDF projection is declared in the entry itself (`rdf`): crm:P2_has_type -> crm:E55_Type when a concept URI is present, nothing when only a label is (`label_only: null`). CRMem 1.6.4 -> 1.6.5 for the companion em:hasDefinition (subproperty of crm:P2_has_type, declared, not emitted by default). Additive only. v1.6.7 (CRMem WIRING, 2026-09-24): rimosso il campo legacy `cidoc_s3d` da tutte le mapping. Non era letto da nessuna parte del codice e portava quattro nomi di classe senza namespace, mai dichiarati e mai emessi: EpochNode = StratigraphicTimeframe; ActivityNodeGroup = StratigraphicActivity; ParadataNodeGroup = ParadataCollection; ResourceNode = ExternalResourceReference. Il prefisso CIDOC-S3D non esiste piu' in nessuno dei due datamodel. v1.6.6 (CIDOC REPAIR, 2026-09-21): classes that pointed at IRIs nobody declares. Checked by parsing the official releases, not from memory. crm:E78_Collection is gone from CIDOC CRM 7.1.3 — renamed E78_Curated_Holding — and E.D. decided NOT to follow the rename, because E78_Curated_Holding is a subclass of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing and a group of nodes is not a physical thing. The three classes that carried it therefore split, each to the class it actually is: GroupNode and RepresentationModelNodeGroup to crm:E73_Information_Object (a conceptual set, and an E90 Symbolic Object, which is what the P106i membership edge needs at both ends), ParadataNodeGroup to crm:E89_Propositional_Object — which is what a gathered body of reasoning IS and what the range of crm:P129i_is_subject_of demands, that being the predicate has_paradata_nodegroup takes in connections 1.6.17 the same day; it stays an E90 through em:NodeGroup, so the membership edge does not break. SemanticShapeNode leaves crmgeo:SP5_Geometric_Place_Expression for crm:E73_Information_Object, PROVVISORIAMENTE: SP5 is not declared at the crmgeo namespace this datamodel emits, crmgeo:SP6_Declarative_Place is the better candidate, and the decision is rinviata da E.D. — E73 commits to nothing meanwhile. crm:P131_is_identified_by, deprecated in CRM 7.x together with E82 Actor Appellation, becomes crm:P1_is_identified_by on AuthorNode (name, surname) and AuthorAINode (name). «CRMs3D» is renamed «CRMem», in components and in referenced_ontology_versions alike: the companion ontology is em.ttl and its namespace is em:, so the old name pointed at nothing anyone could look up. CRMsci moves 3.1 -> 3.2 (latest release). The eight em: terms this file and the connections datamodel cite but em.ttl never defined are now declared there (em:FunctionalUnit, em:GCPSet, em:Narrative, em:NeutralSU, em:RegistrationTransform, em:RepresentationModelNodeGroup, em:hasSubEpoch, em:validatedBy), with domain, range and superclass read off these datamodels and nothing invented. NOT TOUCHED: the `alternative` and legacy `cidoc_s3d` prose fields, which still discuss E78 as an option — prose, not a projection, and rewording them is modelling rather than repair. v1.6.5 (EM16-RMNG, 2026-09-10): adds RepresentationModelNodeGroup, the RM container as a first-class group of the graph — sixth subtype of GroupNode, keeping the parent's E78 Collection because a container IS a curatorial set. Paired with connections datamodel 1.6.14, which adds the is_in_representation_model_group membership edge and widens has_representation_model.target to accept the group. Additive only: no existing entry changed. s3Dgraphy nodes datamodel including node types with CIDOC-CRM mappings. v1.6.4 adds the ADDITIVE georeferencing_nodes section (GCPSetNode = em:GCPSet, RegistrationTransformNode = em:RegistrationTransform, both subclasses of crm:E73_Information_Object with their own extension URIs so the RDF projection stays bijective): the CONTROL and the SOLUTION that place a produced model in the world, introduced with the photogrammetry processing connector. The two modes of that connector are the SHAPE of the graph (a transform with a CRS that has_gcp_set points at = absolute; a transform with crs=null and no control set = a site-local frame; no transform at all = nobody placed it), never a flag. No existing family changed. v1.6.3 re-reads SemanticShapeNode as a PAYLOAD carrier: the proxy of a unit is now a PropertyNode of qualia type 'geometry' that points at the shape (has_semantic_shape), so the proxy inherits the paradata chain it never had. Breaking for consumers that read the proxy as a standalone SemanticShape. v1.6.2 adds AnnotationRegionNode (em:AnnotationRegion, subclass of crm:E36_Visual_Item): the geometry of a 2D annotation in NORMALISED image space, distinct from SemanticShapeNode (3D scene geometry, crmgeo:SP5) - the semantics of the 2D annotator, defined before any canvas exists. v1.6.0 inaugurates a systematic CIDOC-CRM mapping revision: complete audit of all node types against CIDOC-CRM, CRMarchaeo, CRMinf, CRMdig, CRMsci, CRMgeo; replacement of legacy 'cidoc_s3d' pseudo-class names (invented strings without IRI or superclass declaration) with formal em:/s3d: IRIs declared as proper subclasses of CRM classes; introduction of CRMinf as primary (not alternative) for the paradata chain (ParadataNode, PropertyNode interpretive case, ExtractorNode, CombinerNode); introduction of PROV-O for AuthorNode to cover both human and AI agents; alignment with the Heritage Digital Twin Ontology (HDT-O) for containment / granularity properties; LocationNodeGroup (v1.5.3) adopted as the reference pattern (CIDOC-native composition via P2_has_type → E55 Type instances, with explicit extension_status and rationale). Companion deliverables: em.ttl (formal EM extension ontology, dereferenceable via w3id.org/em/) and hdto_extension.ttl (HDT-O granularity properties: contains_HDT, contains_SU, isPrimary). v1.5.4 added RSF (Reused Special Find — spolia) as a stratigraphic subtype, octagon with red border, family=real, is_series=false. Originating DP: DP-26 (spolia project, last DP before the EM 1.5 cut). v1.5.3 added LocationNodeGroup (E53 Place + E55 Type) for spatial / locational membership orthogonal to ActivityNodeGroup (intention) and EpochNode (time). v1.5.2 added family + is_series classification metadata on stratigraphic subtypes.

referenced_ontology_versions._comment: Versions of the reference ontologies this datamodel's mappings are audited against. Update via the mapping-update procedure (see docs: 'Updating the CIDOC mapping') whenever a new official release is adopted.

CRMarchaeo.note: official OWL is internally aligned to CIDOC-CRM 7.1.2 and CRMsci 2.0

spatiotemporal_entities._comment: E.D. 2026-10-10: «Documenti, autori e unità stratigrafiche sono entità spaziotemporali e dovrebbero avere tutto il potenziale e la formalità delle US: start, end, posizione nel grafo matrix». The classes below share the temporal grammar of the Extended Matrix. A subclass is included through its parent (AuthorAINode through AuthorNode, every unit through StratigraphicNode). What they do NOT share is matter: the physical relations (overlies, cuts, fills, abuts, is_bonded_to) and containment (is_part_of) stay between units.

shared.time: absolute_time_start / absolute_time_end, PropertyNodes reached by has_property, with their paradata chain
shared.lanes: has_first_epoch (where the entity begins, which is the lane a client draws it in) and survive_in_epoch (the lanes it lasts through)
shared.sequence: is_after / has_same_time, between any two of them
shared.chronology: Graph.chronology dates the three with the same rules: written, epoch, contained (units only), tpq / taq along the sequence

Node.description: Base class for all nodes in the graph with CIDOC mapping

em_extension.rationale: A DISTINCT uri, not because the base node needs a class of its own in CIDOC terms — it is an E1 and nothing more — but because RDF must be self-describing. Node and UnknownNode both mapped to E1, so their projections were indistinguishable and a reader had to guess which had been written. subclass_of keeps a CRM-only reader seeing the E1.

description.note: 1.6.19 (MICRO la lingua dei dati, decided by E.D. 2026-09-28): the description is TEXT IN A NATURAL LANGUAGE, and leaves in RDF with its language tag (dcterms:description "strato di crollo"@it). Declared here, on the base class, and inherited by every node type: a subclass that writes "description": "P3_has_note" is restating the mapping, not withdrawing the marker (only an explicit natural_language: false would). The language comes in a cascade — the node's data.lang, else the study's working language (GraphNode.data.language), else none — and a language never declared leaves as an untagged literal, counted by the exporter; data.lang 'und' is a language declared unknown and leaves as @und. The NAME is not marked and never will be: US 3014, W5023, USM5023 are identities, not text. An object without kind: node_element, so a mapping note like the strings beside it: no reader turns it into a field to edit. Read by rdf_exporter._Datamodel.is_natural_language, the one place that answers.

lang.note: 1.6.24 (dev30, decided by E.D. 2 Oct 2026, U5): a language RECOGNISED by a tool and confirmed by a person with one gesture is written as data.lang ONLY — no ai_assisted, no record in the graph's register: recognising the language of a text is cleaning of the data, not provenance (s3dgraphy.language.confirm_recognised_language). It is the one explicit exception to the AI marker; every other field a tool proposes keeps it.

created_auth.note: 1.6.21 (dev27, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01, «l'accesso sul campo»): HOW the hand of a signature had entered, beside each signature — created_auth beside created_by, modified_auth beside modified_by, validated_auth beside validated_by: {mode, attested_by?}, mode 'orcid' (verified by ORCID) or 'node_password' (the iD and a password of a StratiGraph node, which attests the identity offline; attested_by = the node's name, required) or, since 1.6.22 (dev28), 'declared' (an iD typed in a tool's preferences, checked by nobody; no attested_by). Through a relay the mode is the relay's, read from the token (crdt.stamp_auth), never the client's declaration. Written by editorial.stamp_created / stamp_modified (auth=), ai_validation.verify (auth=) and the CRDT op's 'auth'; modified_auth follows the last hand and is removed when a new hand comes without one. In RDF: <node>/auth/<created|modified|validated>, reached by em:createdVia / em:modifiedVia / em:validatedVia, with em:authMode and em:attestedBy.

Node.properties_note: 1.6.18: the fields every node may carry in data, beside name and description, and the em: predicate each one leaves with (rdf_exporter: _serialize_editorial, _serialize_ai — called for every node, so declared here on the base class and inherited). created_by / created_at / modified_by / modified_at are the last-hand stamps (editorial.py; an ORCID iD becomes an https://orcid.org/ IRI, anything else a literal); em:createdBy is also written as prov:wasAttributedTo and em:modifiedAt as dcterms:modified. removed.ts / removed.by are the TOMBSTONE (crdt.py, data.removed = {ts, by}). ai_assisted.* is the AI marker (ai_validation.py, data.ai_assisted = {by, model, prompt_ref, fields}): by and prompt_ref are node ids and leave as IRIs, one em:aiAssistedField per touched field, '*' when the marker names none; validated_by / validated_at are the person's verification (em:validatedBy is also prov:wasInfluencedBy). Every one is emitted ONLY when the node carries it. The dotted keys name a member of an object in data (removed.ts is data.removed.ts). Plain strings, so mapping notes and not node elements: no reader turns them into fields to edit. 1.6.20: lang (the node's own data.lang, the first step of the language cascade) leaves as em:originalLanguage, whenever declared — it says which literal is the original once translations (TranslationNode) share its predicate. Not crm:P72_has_language: P72's domain is E33, and the node is not the text.

StratigraphicNode.description: Base class for all stratigraphic units within the graph structure. Inherits from Node and provides additional functionality specific to stratigraphy.

shape.concept: <URI of a SKOS concept in a controlled vocabulary>
shape.label: <the label the recorder saw, carried for display>

definition.description: The DEFINITION of the unit — strato di crollo, riempimento, taglio: the DEFINIZIONE box every US sheet carries (ICCD and the others). An ELEMENT OF THE NODE, like name and description, and NOT a qualia: it is not a PropertyNode reached by has_property, it has no paradata chain of its own, and it lives on the unit (em.json: data.definition, addressable by the CRDT as the field 'data.definition'). The value is a CONCEPT of a controlled vocabulary, not a string: {concept: <uri>, label: <str>} as stratigraph-templates SPEC §1.5 declares for type 'term'. The label is carried only so a reader without the vocabulary still sees a word; the label in the reader's language is RESOLVED AT READING from the concept. Declared here on StratigraphicNode and therefore inherited by every stratigraphic subtype (the RDF exporter walks the class hierarchy). RDF projection, in ONE place — this 'rdf' entry, read by rdf_exporter._serialize_definition: with a concept URI, <unit> <with_concept> <concept> and <concept> rdf:type <concept_class>; with a label and no concept, label_only decides (null = no triple: a bare label is not a concept and inventing an IRI for it would be worse than saying nothing; set it to 'crm:P3_has_note' to keep the word as a note). specialised_alternative names the em: subproperty of crm:P2_has_type declared in em.ttl for the day E.D. wants a definition to be distinguishable from any other P2 type in SPARQL: putting it in with_concept is the one-line switch.

US.label: US (or SU)
US.description: Stratigraphic Unit (SU) or negative stratigraphic unit. Represents a physical stratigraphic unit (positive or negative). It corresponds to an identifiable physical layer or interface in archaeological documentation.

mapping.alternative: E26 Physical Feature + A8 Stratigraphic Unit

values.masonry: A masonry unit — what a recording sheet calls a USM (and pyArchInit's localized codes WSU, MSE, UEM, USZ, ΤΣΜ).
values.coating: A coating unit — plaster, floor, revetment: what a recording sheet calls a USR (rivestimento) or, in English, a USS (surface). The two codes are the same thing in two languages; pyArchInit localizes neither.

stratigraphic_kind.description: The GENRE of a US, when it has one. Absent = an ordinary US, and nothing is written. USM and USR/USS are recording PRACTICES and not categories of the EM language (E.D., 30 Sep 2026): a masonry unit is a US with stratigraphic_kind 'masonry', a coating unit (plaster, floor, revetment) a US with stratigraphic_kind 'coating', and the name keeps saying USM / USR / USS. Recognised on import from the NAME (USM101, 'USR 3', USS12, WSU4…), because the EM yEd palette draws them exactly as a US, and from the TYPE string (xlsx TYPE, pyArchInit unita_tipo: `codes`); a legacy em.json with node_type 'USM', 'USR' or 'USS' opens as US + the kind. `labels` is the English label, translated in datamodel_translations.json (section stratigraphic_kinds). Not projected to RDF yet (rdf: null): the fitting term for masonry is CRMba B5 Stratigraphic Building Unit ⊂ A2, which is not adopted (see the AP21i note in the connections datamodel).

source_code.description: The CODE a US of a kind came in with, when it is not its kind's `default_code` (USS for a coating, WSU for a masonry…). Absent otherwise. It is what goes back to pyArchInit as unita_tipo, so that a USS goes back a USS and not a USR (1.6.13).

USVs.label: USV/s
USVs.description: Structural Virtual Stratigraphic Unit (USV/s). Represents a virtual reconstruction of structural elements, such as walls, columns, or other architectural components that are no longer physically present but can be reconstructed based on archaeological evidence.

mapping.rationale: USVs is a HYPOTHESIZED stratigraphic unit, not physically observed. Multi-typed in OWL as both crminf:I4_Proposition_Set (propositional nature) and crmarchaeo:A8_Stratigraphic_Unit (stratigraphic role). The legacy 'A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit' mapping was semantically wrong (A2 = physical volume). v1.6.0 corrects this via em_extension.

USVn.label: USV/n
USVn.description: Non-structural Virtual Stratigraphic Unit (USV/n). Represents a virtual reconstruction of non-structural elements, such as furniture, decorations, or other non-load bearing components that are no longer physically present but can be reconstructed based on archaeological evidence.

mapping.rationale: Same correction as USVs: virtual = propositional, not physical A2. See em_extension.

SF.label: Special Find
SF.description: Movable physical object whose ORIGINAL position is unknown (and sometimes whose pertinence to the site is uncertain). Distinct from in-situ artefacts — known to exist(ed) but displaced. Architectural artefacts, coins, fragments without findspot. This is also the unit for a REDEPOSITED object: a block in secondary deposition found inside a layer, which is observed where it lies but not where it was made to lie. Provenance / pertinence uncertainty is captured via paradata edges, not by class.

mapping.alternative: E19 Physical Object + crminf:I2_Belief (for uncertain site-pertinence)
mapping.rationale: E19 captures the movable physical-object nature. The 'displacement' semantic (no original-position info) is intrinsic to the EM concept and is captured by the em:DisplacedSpecialFind class; uncertain pertinence to the site is expressed via paradata edges to a crminf:I2_Belief at instance level. Containment in a stratigraphic unit is NOT part of this class: it is carried by the `is_part_of` edge, which since connections 1.6.19 projects to crmarchaeo:AP21i_is_contained_in beside the generic crm:P46i_forms_part_of whenever the container is a US (the only unit that maps to A2). When the WAY the object sits in the deposit has to be stated — embedded since the deposit formed, or intrusive — the CRMarchaeo path is A7 Embedding (AP18/AP19), which is not modelled here and is a declared open point with CRMarchaeo.

SF.scope_note: TWO WORDS THAT ARE NOT THE SAME, and neither is codified in archaeological usage, so EM fixes them here rather than borrowing them. REDEPOSITED: the object arrived where it was found by a process that moved it — collapse, dumping, levelling, erosion — and the layer it sits in post-dates its production. REPOSITIONED: the object has been put back, by us, into a position argued from evidence (anastylosis); that reading belongs to the SF/VSF pair and is what the rest of this manual means by the word. USE SF for both, because in both cases the object is movable and its original position is not given by where it now is. HOW CONTAINMENT IS WRITTEN: a redeposited find inside a layer is an SF joined to that layer by an `is_part_of` edge. Containment is a relation and never a change of node type — the layer stays a US, and the presence of `is_part_of` edges is the only thing that makes it a container. There is no container node type and no 'US node group': the GroupNode family models information sets (E73/E78), which would say somebody GATHERED these objects rather than that the ground holds them. DO NOT USE for an object permanently built into a later structure and not removable without destroying it: that is RSF. The discriminant is structural immobility, not distance travelled. WHAT THE FIND DATES: a redeposited object gives a terminus post quem for the layer that contains it and nothing more; the chronological statement is carried by the epoch edges, not by the containment.

VSF.label: Virtual Special Find
VSF.description: Hypothetical reconstruction of a fragmented Special Find. Virtual reassembly of fragments supported by paradata. Linked to the source fragments (DisplacedSpecialFind instances) via em:reconstructsFrom.

mapping.alternative: E89 Propositional Object + E19 Physical Object
mapping.rationale: E89 (propositional) captures the hypothetical nature; multi-typed with E19 (physical object) because the reconstructed result is referred to as if it were the physical artefact.

RSF.label: Reused Special Find
RSF.description: Re-used architectural or decorative element (spolia) in archaeological reconstructions. A physical object observed in situ but originally produced for a different context — e.g. a Roman column re-used in a medieval church wall. Originating Development Project: DP-26 (spolia, last DP before the EM 1.5 cut).

mapping.alternative: E19 Physical Object + A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit + em:wasReusedFrom (links to original context)
mapping.rationale: Spolia has DUAL nature: an E19 physical object with its own production history AND now an A2 SU embedded in the current stratigraphy. The legacy 'E19 + E11 Modification' alternative captured only the modification-event side; v1.6.0 model spolia as multi-typed E19 + A2 with em:wasReusedFrom pointing to the original (lost) context.

RSF.scope_note: USE for spolia: an element permanently re-incorporated into a later structure and not removable without destroying its host masonry — a Roman column in a medieval wall, a cornice block laid as a doorstep. The discriminant against SF is STRUCTURAL IMMOBILITY, not the fact of having moved. DO NOT USE for a REDEPOSITED object — a block in secondary deposition lying inside a layer: that block is still movable, it was not employed in anything, and it is an SF. The host unit is attached with `is_part_of`, exactly as for a find in a layer; the two cases differ in what the relation MEANS (constituent of a fabric vs. contained in a deposit), which is why the CRMarchaeo refinement AP21i is emitted only when the container is a US.

serSU.label: US series
serSU.description: Series of Stratigraphic Units (SU). A pragmatic stratigraphic aggregation: one logical SU representing multiple physical SUs treated as one (e.g. a series of column bases not worth numbering individually). The series IS itself an SU, not just a collection of SUs.

mapping.alternative: A8 Stratigraphic Unit + P46_is_composed_of (links to component SUs)
mapping.rationale: A series is itself an SU (A8) that aggregates components via P46_is_composed_of. The legacy mapping 'A6 Group Declaration Event' was wrong — A6 is the EVENT of declaring a group, not the group itself.

serUSD.label: USD series
serUSD.description: Series of Documentary Stratigraphic Units (USD). Pragmatic aggregation of multiple DocumentaryVirtualSUs (USD) treated as one logical unit. Same series-as-SU pattern as serSU, applied to the documentary family.

mapping.rationale: Like serSU, but the aggregated components are DocumentaryVirtualSU. Same correction over the legacy A6 mapping.

serUSVn.label: USVn series
serUSVn.description: Series of non-structural Virtual Stratigraphic Units. Pragmatic aggregation of multiple NonStructuralVirtualSU (USVn) treated as one logical unit. Same series-as-SU pattern as serSU.

mapping.rationale: The series IS still a virtual SU (subclass of em:NonStructuralVirtualSU), aggregating its components via P46_is_composed_of. Legacy 'E78 Collection' alone treated the series as a pure collection rather than a typed SU; v1.6.0 keeps the SU nature.

serUSVs.label: USVs series
serUSVs.description: Series of Structural Virtual Stratigraphic Units. Pragmatic aggregation of multiple StructuralVirtualSU (USVs) treated as one logical unit.

mapping.rationale: Same series-as-SU pattern as serUSVn but for the structural virtual family.

USD.label: USD
USD.symbol: white round rectangle with orange border
USD.description: Documentary Stratigraphic Unit. Represents a conceptual stratigraphic unit inferred from historical or documentary sources rather than direct archaeological observation. A USD is the RESULT of a document (an SU posited because a document attests it), NOT a document itself.

mapping.alternative: crminf:I4_Proposition_Set + A8 Stratigraphic Unit (linked to E31 Document via em:derivedFromDocument)
mapping.rationale: A USD is an SU posited on the strength of documentary evidence, not a document. The legacy 'E31 Document' mapping confused the asserted entity with its supporting source. v1.6.0 corrects via em_extension: USD is a Virtual SU (propositional) evidenced by documents.

TSU.label: TSU
TSU.symbol: dotted white rectangle with red border
TSU.description: Transformation Unit. A family of actions modifying a surface or structure — the 'map of degradation' treated stratigraphically. Aggregates multiple A5 Stratigraphic Modification events via P46_is_composed_of.

mapping.rationale: TSU is the canonical 'transformation' / 'degradation' class — A5 in CRMarchaeo. The 'family of actions' aspect is expressed by composition (P46) rather than by a separate class.

UL.label: UL
UL.description: Working Unit. Traces of stone working on architectural surfaces — chisel marks, gradina, iccozza traces on Etruscan tomb walls, hammer impacts. UL is the FEATURE (the marks themselves); the producing event is a separate E12 Production linked via P108i_was_produced_by.

mapping.alternative: E25 Human-Made Feature + P108i_was_produced_by E12 Production
mapping.rationale: UL is the trace, not the act that produced it. v1.6.0 corrects the legacy 'E12 Production' (= the production event itself) to 'E25 Human-Made Feature' (= the observable trace). The production event is modelled separately and linked via P108i. Domain-validated 2026-07-22 (P1-B): E25 Human-Made Feature confirmed — UL is the observable trace; the producing act stays a separate E12 Production via P108i.

BR.label: continuity node
BR.description: End of life of a SU/USV. Marks the point in time when a stratigraphic unit ceases to exist (destruction, dismantling, deep transformation that no longer preserves identity).

mapping.alternative: E64 End of Existence + A5 Stratigraphic Modification (when the end-of-life is itself a stratigraphic modification event)
mapping.rationale: E64 End_of_Existence is the canonical CIDOC class for the cessation event. A5 is an alternative when the cessation is also itself a stratigraphic modification. Domain-validated 2026-07-22 (P1-B): E64 End of Existence confirmed as the canonical cessation event for BR (end of life of a SU/USV).

SE.label: stratigraphic event node
SE.symbol: white triangle with teal border (#2A8C8C) — famiglia cromatica delle attivita: un SE e un atto, non materia. Deciso in S10 (2026-08-02); prima era 'to be defined'.
SE.description: An event that creates, modifies, or destroys a stratigraphic unit (e.g. an earthquake causing a plaster collapse, an act of demolition, the start of construction). Distinct from the resulting unit itself: an SE is the PROCESS, the SU is the result. Can be enriched by a 3D simulation (em:RepresentationModel) of the event. May be paired with its resulting unit to provide a temporal range bracketing the action.

mapping.alternative: A4 Stratigraphic Genesis (when the event creates a unit or an interface) + E64 End of Existence (paired with the BR node for the destroyed unit's end of life)
mapping.rationale: Changed 2026-07-11 (was generic E5 Event): A5 Stratigraphic Modification covers the whole SE span within CRMarchaeo. Formation is A4 (A4 is a subclass of A5); modification is A5 itself; destruction is A5-as-disturbance (AP8 disturbed) plus, for the cut it produces, A4 genesis of the A3 interface. Cf. Guillem et al. 2024 (SWODCH), which models genesis events as A4 with AP7_produced. E5 remains reachable transitively (A5 is a subclass of S18 Alteration, itself a subclass of E5). See WP3 coverage analysis, Appendix D.1.

USN.label: US-
USN.description: Negative Stratigraphic Unit (US negativa, displayed 'US-') — a lacuna produced by a SUBTRACTION of matter: a pit cut, an opening broken through a wall, an erosion surface, a levelling. What defines it is the destructive act, which is what separates it from the NEUTRAL unit (USNt), a void that was never filled because it was never meant to be. Equally observable on the ground as a positive unit, hence the `real` family. POL6 (2026-08-04): the token is USN again — the historical spelling of this library and of what pyArchInit vendors, and the one that reads as the Italian 'US Negativa'. POL5 had briefly moved it to 'USNeg' to free USN for the neutral unit; that made a token spell one thing and mean another, and put the two projects in disagreement about a three-letter word.
USN.scope_note: USE when matter that WAS there has been taken away, and you can name the act: a cut, a pit, an opening broken through masonry, an erosion surface, a levelling or shaving of a structure. The relation to the unit it removes is a stratigraphic one and all of them are available (`cuts`, `fills`, `abuts`, sequence, …) — this is a unit of the sequence and behaves like one. DO NOT USE for a void left deliberately by the act of building (a window opening, a niche, a room): that is USNt, the neutral unit, and calling it negative dates it to a removal that never happened.

mapping.alternative: A3 Stratigraphic Interface + A5 Stratigraphic Modification (the producing removal event)
mapping.rationale: A negative SU is an INTERFACE (A3) produced by removal of matter, not a positive volumetric SU (A2) — a REAL CRMarchaeo class, not a placeholder: the surface left by a cut is exactly what A3 models. The legacy 'A8 Stratigraphic Unit (Negative)' was not a real CRMarchaeo class. The removal action is a separate A5 event linked via P108i_was_produced_by.

USNt.label: USNt
USNt.symbol: grey outline at the four corners only (no continuous border)
USNt.description: Neutral Stratigraphic Unit (Unità Stratigrafica Neutra, USNt) — a void that is part of the DESIGN and not the product of a destruction: the `risparmi` of masonry, a window or door opening, a niche, the empty volume of a room. The wall was built around it, so nothing was ever removed. The distinction from the negative unit (USN, displayed 'US-') is stratigraphic and not cosmetic: a demolition void is evidence of an ACT, a risparmio is evidence of an INTENTION, and reading one as the other dates the void to a removal that never happened. Added in POL5 (2026-08-04) on E.D.'s explicit authorisation; the token became USNt in POL6, when USN went back to the negativa.
USNt.scope_note: USE for a void produced BY the act of building: window and door openings, niches, the volume enclosed by walls, any gap left deliberately in a masonry face — an absence that was WANTED. DO NOT USE for a cut, an opening broken through an existing wall, an erosion surface or a levelling: those are USN (US-), because matter was removed. DO NOT USE for a gap in the DOCUMENTATION (something not observed): that is not a stratigraphic unit at all. Test: if you can name the action that removed the matter, it is USN; if the matter was never there, it is USNt.

attach_rules._comment: E.D.'s constraint, and the reason for it: a risparmio cannot cut, fill, abut or be bonded to anything — nothing was removed and nothing touches it — so the only stratigraphic statement it can carry is sequence. `is_after` covers both directions (its declared `reverse` is is_before). NB the constraint belongs to the NEUTRAL unit only: the negative one (USN) is a unit of the sequence and keeps every relation. The enforceable copy lives in s3Dgraphy_connections_datamodel.json -> node_type_restrictions.USNt, which is what consumers read; this field is the same fact stated where a reader of the node type will look for it.
attach_rules.paradata: unrestricted — a risparmio is documented, measured and reasoned about like any other unit (has_property, has_data_provenance, is_in_paradata_nodegroup, epoch and group membership are all unaffected).

mapping.alternative: A3 Stratigraphic Interface + A4 Stratigraphic Genesis (a CONSTRUCTIVE genesis, not the A5 destructive modification the negative unit gets)
mapping.rationale: TENTATIVE placeholder, better informed than POL5's E24 but still not a decision. TODO CIDOC: USNt (risparmio) — probabile A3_Stratigraphic_Interface con genesi COSTRUTTIVA (A4_Stratigraphic_Genesis), distinta dalla negativa che nasce da una A5 distruttiva. NON e detto sia una classe nuova: E.D. coordina con Achille Felicetti / CRMarchaeo. The reading behind the placeholder: what is observable is a SURFACE bounding an absence, which is what A3 models, and the difference from the negative unit is not the surface but its genesis — built, not cut. If that holds, the two share A3 and differ in the event that produced them, and no new class is needed; POL5's E24 said less and claimed more. MUST be confirmed before any RDF export claims to be CRMarchaeo-conformant.

EpochNode.label: Epoch
EpochNode.description: Node representing a temporal epoch. It is a convenient grouping that allows attributing a series of actions to a temporal delta. Once the specific chronology data, expressed as start_time and end_time properties of individual SUs, is defined through dating elements, these epoch nodes are ignored where such specific data are available.

GroupNode.description: Node that represents a group of nodes. These groups can be of various types: see subclasses below.

em_extension.rationale: Superclass of the EM grouping axes (activity, paradata, timebranch, location, functional unit). It shared E78 with ParadataNodeGroup, so a generic group and a paradata group projected identically. REPAIR 2026-09-21: crm:E78_Collection is not declared in CIDOC CRM 7.1.3 — the class was renamed E78_Curated_Holding, so the IRI emitted here was inert. E.D. decided NOT to follow the rename: E78_Curated_Holding is a subclass of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing, and a group of nodes is not a physical thing. E73 Information Object is the conceptual set: it is an E90 Symbolic Object, which is what P106i_forms_part_of (the membership edge is_in_paradata_nodegroup) requires at both ends.

ActivityNodeGroup.label: Activity Node Group
ActivityNodeGroup.description: Group node for activities. An activity is a logical group of actions that are kept together for a narrative purpose and information order (e.g., construction of a room of a building in year x, restoration activities of various parts of that room 20 years later).

ParadataNodeGroup.label: Paradata Node Group
ParadataNodeGroup.description: Group node for paradata. This group brings together all paradata related to a stratigraphic unit: typically named '[US_name]_PD' (ParaData).

em_extension.rationale: The paradata of one stratigraphic unit gathered as a unit ('[US]_PD'). A distinct uri makes 'give me the paradata groups' a type query rather than a naming convention. REPAIR 2026-09-21: crm:E78_Collection is not declared in CIDOC CRM 7.1.3 — the class was renamed E78_Curated_Holding, so the IRI emitted here was inert. E.D. decided NOT to follow the rename: E78_Curated_Holding is a subclass of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing, and a group of nodes is not a physical thing. E89 Propositional Object is what a gathered body of reasoning IS, and it is what the range of crm:P129i_is_subject_of demands — the predicate has_paradata_nodegroup now carries (repaired the same day). It stays an E90 Symbolic Object through em:NodeGroup (E73), so the P106i membership edge keeps its range.

TimeBranchNodeGroup.label: Time Branch Node Group
TimeBranchNodeGroup.description: An alternative timeline aggregating a set of mutually exclusive beliefs about a temporal interval. Two TimeBranch instances can be connected via em:contrastsWith (symmetric) to express alternative reconstructions of the same period. The Period nature (E4) anchors temporal identity; the alternative-set semantic is captured by contrastsWith.

mapping.rationale: E4 Period anchors the temporal identity. The 'alternative set of beliefs' aspect is NOT modeled as I2 Belief (everything in EM is propositional by design) but as a symmetric contrastsWith relation between TimeBranches. This avoids over-typing every aggregator as a Belief.

LocationNodeGroup.label: Location Node Group
LocationNodeGroup.description: Group node for spatial / locational membership of stratigraphic units and paradata. Orthogonal to ActivityNodeGroup (intention) and EpochNode (time): a Location answers the question 'what (named) place is this in?'. Three required kinds coexist on the same axis: 'toponym' (external/administrative identity, e.g. Pompei), 'study' (operational/procedural identity, e.g. Saggio4/A2) and 'functional' (interpretive/semantic identity, e.g. Casa del Fauno / Room 12). Propagation is additive: multiple memberships compose, none overrides — distinct from EpochNode which is substitutive (finest-grained wins). Membership is m:n via multiple is_in_location edges; the optional 'is_primary: true' attribute on one edge marks the membership rendered as a yEd group folder in em-graph. Locations are hierarchical: a LocationNodeGroup can itself be is_in_location of another LocationNodeGroup. A Location is identitary, not geometric: for coordinates / EPSG / shifts use GeoPositionNode (linked at the CIDOC level via P161).

mapping.alternative: E53 Place + E55 Type (kind classifier via P2_has_type)
mapping.rationale: No new s3d:Location class is introduced. A LocationNodeGroup is a pure CIDOC E53 Place; its three epistemic planes (toponym/study/functional) are expressed by classification with E55 Type instances (P2_has_type), which is the CIDOC-native pattern. CRMarchaeo does not introduce a Place-level container distinct from E53, so plain E53 is preferred.

em_extension.rationale: Revises the mapping rationale above on ONE point: the CIDOC modelling is unchanged (this IS an E53 Place classified by E55 Type), but a plain E53 was shared with GeoPositionNode, and the two are opposites — a Location is identitary ('what named place is this in?'), a GeoPosition is metric (an origin, a CRS, an azimuth). One class for both made the projection ambiguous, readable only by looking for shift triples, which a GeoPosition without a transform does not have.

kind.description: Epistemic plane of the location. 'toponym' = external/administrative identity (Pompei, Lazio, Italia); 'study' = operational/procedural identity (saggio, settore, quadrato, sondage); 'functional' = interpretive/semantic identity (basilica, room A, courtyard). The three coexist on the same node and may compose.

mapping.pattern: The E53 Place is classified via P2_has_type by exactly one of three reserved E55 Type instances. CIDOC-native composition; no new property URI is introduced.

toponym.rationale: Names the toponym epistemic plane. CIDOC-core has no reserved E55 Type instance for the administrative/external-identity discrimination of an archaeological place; CRMarchaeo does not introduce equivalent type categorisations either. Candidate primitive for a forthcoming CIDOC-S3D extension.

study.rationale: Names the study/operational plane (saggio, settore, quadrato, sondage). No CIDOC-core or CRMarchaeo equivalent — CRMarchaeo carries process semantics on the activity side but not as a Place-classifying type. Candidate primitive for a forthcoming CIDOC-S3D extension.

functional.rationale: Names the functional/interpretive plane (basilica, room A, courtyard). No CIDOC-core or CRMarchaeo equivalent. Candidate primitive for a forthcoming CIDOC-S3D extension.

propagation.description: Declarative rule for how location membership propagates to descendants. Location is additive (memberships compose; none overrides), distinct from EpochNode which is substitutive (finest-grained wins).

mapping.serialization: em:propagation literal on the node, ONLY when it is not the default 'additive' (rdf_exporter, LocationNodeGroup branch, since c1a702c 2026-08-12); read back by the RDF importer. No triple means additive.
mapping.rationale: Propagation is a rule for how a graph traversal composes memberships, and the default is declared here, at the schema level, so a node saying 'the usual' writes nothing. A node that departs from it (substitutive) changes what its membership MEANS, and that is a fact about the node which must survive the RDF round-trip: hence the literal for the exception. 1.6.18: this entry said 'not serialized to triplestore', written before the exporter began to emit the exception (c1a702c); the code is what happens, so the entry now says it.

FunctionalUnitNodeGroup.label: Functional Unit
FunctionalUnitNodeGroup.description: Typed aggregation of the stratigraphic units that make up one recognisable functional/architectural component — the column made of its US, the wall made of its US (DP-72). Answers what a set of units IS, as a building component. Built BOTTOM-UP from the stratigraphic reading: the member units stay intact and fully stratigraphic underneath, each keeping its own epochs, paradata and provenance. Membership is a TAG axis, 'is_in_functional_unit' (m:n, additive), NOT the nesting axis 'is_part_of': the relation is the same mereological P46i, but a Functional Unit legitimately SPANS EPOCHS (a wall built across four of them still carries the roof as one body) and a swimlane box cannot, so the functional reading lives in its own view beside pure stratigraphy without either constraining the other. NOT an ActivityNodeGroup (DP-43: a cluster of actions/processes — what was DONE, not what the units ARE); NOT a generic container (DP-36: a US/USD/VSF acting as container is still a stratigraphic unit with its own formation event, while a Functional Unit has none of its own); NOT a LocationNodeGroup of kind 'functional' (a named PLACE answering 'where', not a COMPONENT answering 'what'); NOT a geometric construction grammar (the geometry type travels BY REFERENCE via 'geometry_type_ref', nothing internalized). Attach rules: members StratigraphicNode --is_in_functional_unit--> FunctionalUnit; nesting FunctionalUnit --is_in_functional_unit--> FunctionalUnit (the capital inside the column); FunctionalUnit --is_part_of--> US stays legal and means the whole component PHYSICALLY EMBEDDED in a stratigraphic unit (a column engaged in a later wall). The orthogonal axes stay orthogonal: a member keeps its own has_first_epoch / is_in_activity / is_in_location, and the Functional Unit has NO epoch of its own — its temporal extent is DERIVED from its members and may cover several epochs. EM manual: 'SU / USD / VSF as Container' (Stratigraphic Nodes) and the is_part_of connector.

mapping.alternative: E24 Physical Human-Made Thing + P46_is_composed_of (its member units)
mapping.rationale: A Functional Unit asserts a made THING composed of its parts, so it takes the physical class and the mereological P46, NOT the E78 Collection its GroupNode parent defaults to: E78 is a curatorial set (what someone gathered), while a component is a whole made of parts. It is likewise not E7 Activity (that is the ActivityNodeGroup axis: the act, not the thing) nor E53 Place (the LocationNodeGroup axis: where, not what). Same precedent as TimeBranchNodeGroup, which overrides the E78 default with E4 Period. E24 rather than E22/E25 keeps both movable components and immobile features in scope without over-committing. The target mapping to CRMvr V5 Component Element is separate work (DP-72).

geometry_type_ref.description: Opaque pointer into an EXTERNAL geometry-type taxonomy (bSDD / Getty AAT / an HBIM shape-grammar vocabulary). Free-form by design: no vocabulary is internalized or validated by s3Dgraphy, and the geometric construction grammar stays with the modeller / OpenBIM at export time (DP-72).

mapping.rationale: A typological classification of the component, carried by reference to an external authority rather than by an internal enumeration. The concrete field shape (scheme + id, or a plain URI) is not fixed yet — see DP-72.

RepresentationModelNodeGroup.label: RM Container
RepresentationModelNodeGroup.description: Typed aggregation of the representation models that form ONE named set published under a single Document — «Survey 2015» under D.01, «Reconstruction» under D.09 (EM16-RMNG, meeting of 2026-09-10). Until then the RM container lived only as EM Tools' `scene.rm_containers` PropertyGroup, so the grouping that gives the set its meaning was invisible to anyone reading the graph. IT SITS BESIDE, IT DOES NOT REPLACE: every member keeps its own epoch edges (has_first_epoch / survive_in_epoch) and the Document keeps its DIRECT has_representation_model edges to each model — the group is added on top and never put in between, so a consumer that ignores it reads exactly what it read before. Membership is the TAG axis 'is_in_representation_model_group', like is_in_functional_unit and is_in_location, but 1:1 and not m:n: a mesh belongs to exactly one container, the rule already in force on the Blender side where `mesh_names` is authoritative. A group may legally be EMPTY and may legally have NO Document: both are states the RM Manager UI already shows. NOT a FunctionalUnitNodeGroup (that aggregates stratigraphic units into a building component; these members are models, not units); NOT an ActivityNodeGroup (nothing happened here and the set has no formation event of its own); NOT the Document, which stays the documentary anchor — deleting the container removes the group and not the Document.

mapping.rationale: REPAIR 2026-09-21: reads E73 Information Object, inherited from GroupNode, because crm:E78_Collection is not declared in CIDOC CRM 7.1.3 (renamed E78_Curated_Holding, which is physical — see GroupNode). The argument below is kept because it is still the reason this subtype does NOT override its parent; only the class the parent carries has changed. — The E78 Collection its GroupNode parent defaults to is the RIGHT class here, and this is the one group subtype that does not override it: an RM container IS a curatorial set — what somebody gathered and published under one document — which is exactly what E78 says. That is the difference from FunctionalUnitNodeGroup, which overrides to E24 because a component is a made thing composed of parts rather than a set somebody assembled, and from TimeBranchNodeGroup, which overrides to E4 Period. NOTE: this says nothing about where `digital representation of` grafts (the model↔thing relation, P138i / CIDOC-S3D:has3DRepresentation and the CRMdig neighbourhood) — that is left open as D3 in the 2026-09-10 spec and reserved for E.D.

ParadataNode.description: Base class for nodes representing the reasoning chain (paradata) supporting an assertion. Not a document — the documentation lives at the source end of the chain (DocumentNode reached via ExtractorNode → CombinerNode → Paradata).

mapping.alternative: crminf:I1_Argumentation + E31 Document (for the document that records the argument)
mapping.rationale: ParadataNode is the HEAD of an argumentation chain — semantically a crminf:I1_Argumentation, NOT a document (E31). The legacy E31 mapping conflated the argument with the documentation about it. v1.6.0 promotes CRMinf to primary for the paradata chain (ParadataNode, ExtractorNode, CombinerNode).

PropertyNode.label: Property
PropertyNode.description: Node representing a property (qualia) of another node. The CIDOC class is CONDITIONAL on the qualia type — looked up at serialization time in em_qualia_types.json: dimensional qualia (height/width/weight) → E54_Dimension, typology qualia (color/style) → E55_Type, material → E57_Material, interpretive qualia (aesthetic_value) → crminf:I4_Proposition_Set. PropertyNode itself is the structural shell (em:Qualia); the semantic class comes from the qualia type catalogue.

mapping.alternative: DEPENDS ON property_type — see em_qualia_types.json: physical_material.dimensional → E54_Dimension; physical_material.material → E57_Material; cultural_interpretive.semantic → crminf:I4_Proposition_Set; functional → E55_Type; etc.
mapping.rationale: PropertyNode is a generic shell — its specific CRM class depends on the qualia it expresses. The RDF exporter resolves this conditionally (em.ttl declares em:Qualia as E1 placeholder; the qualia-specific class is added at serialization). Domain-validated 2026-07-22 (P1-B): E1 CRM Entity is the INTENDED qualia-refined fallback, not a missing mapping — the concrete CIDOC class comes from em_qualia_types.json `mappings.cidoc_crm` per property_type (height→E54, color/functional→E55, material→E57, interpretive→crminf:I4), resolved by rdf_exporter.get_qualia_crm_iri.

DocumentNode.label: Document
DocumentNode.description: Node that represents a document or source. Attributes: data (dict): Additional metadata, such as 'url_type'.

spatiotemporal.start: when the document comes into being (absolute_time_start): written, drawn, photographed, surveyed
spatiotemporal.end: when it ceases to be available as the thing it was (absolute_time_end): lost, destroyed, superseded; absent for a document that is still there
spatiotemporal.lane: has_first_epoch: the epoch where it is born, which is where the canonical document is drawn and what its instances' badge names; survive_in_epoch the epochs it lasts through
spatiotemporal.sequence: is_after / has_same_time with units, other documents and authors: a report is after the excavation it reports

ExtractorNode.label: Extractor
ExtractorNode.description: Node that represents the act of extracting information / adopting a belief FROM a single source (DocumentNode). The mediator between a source and an assertion: 'I adopted this belief because the source says so'. Distinct from CombinerNode which combines MULTIPLE extractions.

mapping.rationale: I7 Belief Adoption in CRMinf is the exact CRM-side counterpart of an extractor: the act of adopting a belief from a single piece of evidence. The legacy E7 Activity was too generic — it captured the activity but lost the epistemic nuance.

CombinerNode.label: Combiner
CombinerNode.description: Node that represents the act of combining MULTIPLE extracted beliefs into a single conclusion. The 'X and Y therefore Z' step in the EM paradata chain: combiner takes multiple ExtractorNode inputs and produces a synthesized assertion. Distinct from ExtractorNode (single-source belief adoption).

mapping.rationale: I5 Inference Making in CRMinf is exactly the act of producing a conclusion from premises — the CRM-side counterpart of EM's combiner. The legacy E7 was too generic.

GeoPositionNode.label: Geo Position
GeoPositionNode.description: Class to represent a GeoPosition node in the graph. Attributes: type (str): Node type, set to 'geo_position'. data (dict): Data related to geographic position.
GeoPositionNode.node_usage: ONE PER GRAPH, not per epoch: georeferencing is a property of the GRAPH (like its name, author, licence, HR id — the graph-level metadata), so Graph.__init__ auto-creates a single node with id 'geo_<graph_id>' and the em.json importer drops that synthetic one when the document carries its own. The SHIFT IS THE ANCHOR, NOT THE POSITION: shift_x/y/z are the origin of the scene-local system expressed in the CRS named by epsg — the point that is (0,0,0) in the scene — and may legitimately sit OUTSIDE the geometry (a round grid vertex hundreds of metres from the monument). It is therefore NOT where a map marker belongs: the marker goes on the CENTROID of the geometry (api.georeference_scene). 'rotation' is the scene azimuth in degrees, clockwise from the GRID north of the CRS epsg (D2, decided by E.D. 4 Oct 2026: not the geographic north — between the two lies the meridian convergence, which one graph never applies and two graphs meet only as their relative convergence), 0 = north up (the default and the normal case); data.rotation_reference = 'grid' says it in the data. The scene-local → geo transform is: rotate by rotation, add the shift, reproject epsg → 4326 (api.reproject). Graph-side twin of EMTools' scene.em_georef (georef_manager), which propagates the same values to BlenderGIS and 3DSC.

em_extension.rationale: The metric anchor of the graph: a CRS, an origin (shift) and an azimuth. Distinct from em:LocationNodeGroup, the identitary side of place — the two shared E53 and could only be told apart by the presence of shift triples, an inference that fails for a graph georeferenced without a transform.

rotation_reference.note: 1.6.25 (D2, decided by E.D. 4 Oct 2026): the north 'rotation' is measured from — always 'grid' (the grid north of the CRS epsg), written by GeoPositionNode and set on load when a document does not carry it (it is the definition, not a guess). Not projected to RDF: the anchor's frame is the CRS itself.

ResourceNode.label: Link
ResourceNode.description: Class to represent a link node (ResourceNode) in the graph. Attributes: url (str): URL of the link. url_type (str): Type of URL (e.g., 'External link', 'Image'). description (str): Description of the link.

mapping.alternative: E73 Information Object + E36 Visual Item

packaging.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): how the bytes are packed (file | file_set | directory | archive | datablock, the dtcstamp PACKAGINGS), DECLARED — never the effective_packaging fallback. Emitted only when recorded. 1.6.24 (dev30): the vocabulary with its labels lives here (values, labels; translations in datamodel_translations.json, section packagings), so an interface reads the name of a packaging from the datamodel instead of its own words.

values.file: One file: the resource is its bytes.
values.file_set: A few files that call each other (obj → mtl → textures, gltf → bin, shp and companions): the resource is the list of its members, stamped by the digest of that list.
values.directory: A folder: the resource is everything under it, members reached by has_file with their relative path.
values.archive: One file that packs others (zip, .3tz): the resource is the archive's bytes.
values.datablock: One object inside a file (a blend:// locator): comparable by a structural digest, not verifiable by downloading.

tier.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): master | distribution | …, declared; emitted only when recorded.

digest_covers.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): what em:checksum covers — artifact (the bytes), payload, members (the canonical list of the members of a file_set, dtcstamp.members_digest). add_resource writes members for a file_set; a legacy members_digest equal to the checksum leaves as members.

members_digest.note: 1.6.24 (dev30, decided by E.D. 2 Oct 2026, D4): NOT A SECOND FIELD — the digest of a file_set is its checksum with digest_covers members (dtcstamp.members_digest of the list of members, A1 of dev29). In RDF it leaves ALSO as em:membersDigest, a predicate of its own, so a reader tells the digest of a set from the digest of a file without reading em:checksum and em:digestCovers together; those two stay, for compatibility. A TTL carrying only em:membersDigest comes back as checksum + digest_covers members.

content_digest.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): the digest of the CONTENT of a tree (a folder or its .3tz), dtcstamp.content_digest — the same for both forms. 1.6.24 (dev30, decided by E.D. 2 Oct 2026, D7): also the digest of the DATA of a master that lives inside another file — for a Metashape model (a datablock, psx://) the sha256 of its mesh.ply inside the project's model.zip, written by importer.metashape_project. It is COMPARED (has the master changed?), never verified by downloading, and so it is never the checksum, which is the digest of bytes one can fetch.

addresses.note: 1.6.21 (dev27, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01, «più risorse per un documento»): the SAME bytes — the same digest — are ONE resource with several addresses (the same PDF on the disk, on MinIO, on Zenodo); different manifestations are sister resources. data.addresses = [{locator, residency?, checked_at?, ok?}], written only when there is a second address or a check; address 0 is data.url, which a consumer that knows only url keeps reading. ok true = reachable at checked_at, false = dead (a warning while a live one remains, never removed by a check), absent = never checked. Written by s3dgraphy.resources.addresses (add_address refuses a different digest, and a resource with no digest). In RDF every locator is an rdfs:seeAlso of the resource, and each address <resource>/address/<i> em:hasAddress, with em:locator, em:residency, em:checkedAt, em:reachable.

checksum_at.note: 1.6.21 (dev27): the instant a DATED digest was taken — s3dgraphy.resources.addresses.snapshot_uri downloads the page a reference points at and gives it checksum + checksum_at, because a page changes and the digest says of which day it is.

lang.note: 1.6.21 (dev27, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01, «il testo, la risorsa e la selezione»): on a RESOURCE, data.lang is the language of the CONTENT of the file — what it is made of — not the language of the resource's own description: a Latin PDF does not make its Italian description Latin. One BCP 47 tag, or a sorted list for more («latino e italiano a fronte» = ["it", "la"]), written by s3dgraphy.language.set_content_languages. It does NOT enter the cascade of the language of the texts (language.node_language skips resources and their files), it is not written at birth, and it leaves as one dcterms:language per tag instead of em:originalLanguage. The DocumentNode is the WORK, with no text in its fields; the resources are its manifestations, the text is in the file; the ExtractorNode is the selection, with the original words of the passage in its description and its own data.lang.

lod_level.note: 1.6.25 (D1, decided by E.D. 4 Oct 2026, TASSONOMIA-TIER-3D §2a): the LEVEL of a version of an asset, an ordinal INSIDE ONE derivation chain. The master is tier = master and has no level; lod0 is the first version derived from it that one can work on (textured with the Demetrescu-D'Annibale formula: 1.26 mm per texel side, 4096² atlases, UV ratio 0.6 — Demetrescu et al. 2026, Remote Sensing 18, 203, §2 and §4.7); lod1…lodN count the lod_generation steps from LOD0 (as 3DSC's LOD generator does), a version that only reduces its textures included. COMPUTED from the chain (dtc_derived_from + lod_generation, resources.versions.lod_level_of), never stored in the graph: WRITTEN only when the graph leaves (em.json, manifest, record, RDF) and at load computed again and compared, like a checksum (check_lod_levels): a difference is a line in the Log. Why still «measures, not an enumeration of levels»: the etiquette orders one chain and means nothing outside it; the measures compare chains. Engines' automatic LOD (Nanite) is one more way to show a version and does not replace the chain.

values.analysis: Study and measure on the model: digital autopsy of the units, survey, sections, scientific annotation.
values.realtime: Interactive exploration in an engine (Unreal, Unity, Godot, EMviq), desktop and HMD, open world.
values.web: Viewing in the browser (ATON, Heriverse, Voyager), streamed too.
values.render: Non-interactive products: plates, sections, reconstructive views, CGI video.
values.preview: Light preview for catalogues and records.
values.heriverse: A version made for Heriverse: the package on disk (em.json and its versions) Heriverse opens offline, or the one it takes first from the node (1.6.26, H4).
values.aton: A version made for an ATON app: the same package, for an ATON viewer other than Heriverse (1.6.26, H4).

use._note: 1.6.26 (H4): heriverse and aton, a version made for a viewer; the version for a use is chosen by ONE rule, choose_version, whose cases (JSON_config/version_for_cases.json) Heriverse passes too. 1.6.25 (D1, TASSONOMIA-TIER-3D §2b): what a version is FOR, a LIST (one version can serve the browser and the engine — unlike Voyager, which gives one usage per derivative). Correspondences, from the taxonomy's table: analysis — Voyager none (Editorial3D/Highest undocumented), 3D Tiles none; realtime — Voyager usage App3D; web — Voyager usage Web3D with quality Low/Medium/High, 3D Tiles: the tileset is the usual container and the level is chosen by geometricError; mobile_ar — Voyager quality AR and usage iOSApp3D; print — Voyager usage Print3D; render — Voyager usage Image2D (the correspondence is ours, not Voyager's); preview — Voyager quality Thumb. 'archive' is left out: keeping is the master's reason to be (tier = master). The older single 'purpose' of a lod_generation step is read as a one-item list when it is one of these.

tris_per_m2.note: 1.6.25 (D1): a measure of a version, computed by EMtools when the version is born. Triangles per square metre of surface: a MEASURE, with no target (Demetrescu et al. 2026 record 955–5403 on Amba Aradam).

texel_density_dd.note: 1.6.25 (D1): a measure of a version, computed by EMtools when the version is born. The texel SIDE in mm, in the form of the Demetrescu-D'Annibale formula (reference 1.26 mm; surface / (atlases × side² × UV ratio), square root).

texture_count.note: 1.6.25 (D1): a measure of a version, computed by EMtools when the version is born. How many texture atlases.

texture_side_px.note: 1.6.25 (D1): a measure of a version, computed by EMtools when the version is born. The side of an atlas in pixels (4096 in the reference).

uv_ratio.note: 1.6.25 (D1): a measure of a version, computed by EMtools when the version is born. The share of the atlas the UV islands fill (0.6 in the reference).

reduction_from_lod0.note: 1.6.25 (D1): a measure of a version, computed by EMtools when the version is born. The reduction from LOD0 (triangles of this version / triangles of LOD0) — 3DSC's «magnitude».

geometric_error_m.note: 1.6.25 (D1): a measure of a version, computed by EMtools when the version is born. For a 3D Tiles tileset only: its geometricError, in metres.

ResourceFileNode.label: Resource file
ResourceFileNode.description: ONE FILE of a resource (E.D. 2026-09-30, «la risorsa e i suoi file»): the ResourceNode is the SET — the handle a person stamps, cites and opens, with name, kind, scope, residency, role, tier, packaging and rights — and the ResourceFileNode is each member: an obj, its mtl and its textures are three files of one resource. Reached by has_file (reverse is_file_of); the ROLE (entry_point | member) and the RELATIVE PATH travel on the EDGE, because the same file (a corrected texture) sits in N resources under N paths. With ONE file the node is IMPLICIT: a ResourceNode with url (and checksum) and no has_file is a resource of one file, and s3dgraphy.resources.files.resource_files shows that file anyway; the node is written only when there are several files or the one file has a stamp or an identity of its own. Fields: url (a path, a file:// / s3:// / http(s):// URI or a blend:// locator), checksum ('sha256:<hex>'; 'emstruct1:<hex>' for a datablock, comparable not verifiable), size_bytes, media_type. For a datablock blend_file and datablock are READ from the blend:// locator (resources/resolver.py, the one place that knows its form), never stored twice. The same file in several resources is ONE node, recognised by its checksum.

mapping.rationale: crmdig:D1_Digital_Object (CRMdig 5.0, ⊂ E73 Information Object): a file is an identifiable digital object, and the set it belongs to is the E73 the ResourceNode already is; the membership is P106_is_composed_of on has_file, E90 → E90, which both satisfy. The role and the path are edge data and do not project.

em_extension.rationale: A DISTINCT uri: a DTC output ResourceNode is already co-typed crmdig:D1_Digital_Object, so a file typed D1 alone would read back as a resource. subclass_of keeps a CRMdig-only reader seeing the D1.

RepresentationModelNode.label: Representation Model
RepresentationModelNode.description: 3D representation (model or spatialized image) of a stratigraphic node — real or virtual. Always linked to the represented node via crm:P138_represents.

mapping.alternative: D1 Digital Object + SP6 Declarative Place + E52 Time-Span
mapping.rationale: D1 (Digital Object) from CRMdig is the canonical class for any digital asset. Multi-typed with SP6/E52 when the representation carries spatial and temporal anchoring.

RepresentationModelDocNode.label: Representation Model Document
RepresentationModelDocNode.description: 3D representation of a documentary node — e.g. a historical photo georeferenced and positioned in 3D space at the location it depicts. Linked via crm:P138_represents to a DocumentNode (or ExtractorNode/CombinerNode that uses the document). Specialization of em:RepresentationModel.
RepresentationModelDocNode.scope_note: RM of an asset that CANNOT sit in 3D without a transformation matrix — (0,0,0) is an improbable place for it — and that normally involves a POV / camera sighting the document (a section, an elevation, an image); typically a georeferenced 2D document used as a base. It is NOT the RMDoc case when a photogrammetric model is used as a SOURCE: that is an RM bound to its epoch, plus a Document. An asset that is already 3D and already an RM does NOT generate an RMDoc. The family reads as a parallel of spatial instances of conceptual nodes: proxy:US :: RMSF:SF :: RM:state :: RMDoc:Document. What has degrees on an RMDoc is the SPATIALISATION, not the existence: the document certainly exists, and its temporality is an attribution (certain, or argued through a paradata chain) — never a grade on the geometry axis. The position itself (X,Y,Z + rotation) lives here and nowhere else; the Document may mirror the geometry value on its yEd border for diagram convenience but carries no position.

placement_qualia.note: Scale of METRIC AUTHORITY OF PLACEMENT, most to least. 'symbolic' (EM 1.6, Q-C) is the lowest rung: the base is not metric at all (not-to-scale map, schematic plan, sketch). 'em_based' sits outside the ladder — it is a provenance statement (the asset IS an EM-derived reconstruction), which says nothing about how well it is placed.

from_document.note: The Document is the attach target. An RMDoc is NOT bound to an epoch nor to a stratigraphic unit — that is what separates it from an RM.

to_resource.note: The P67 hinge to the file on disk goes through the ResourceNode, as for every other representation facet.

mapping.alternative: D1 Digital Object + P138 to DocumentNode
mapping.rationale: Subclass of em:RepresentationModel; the specific kind of target (document) is enforced structurally rather than as a flat property.

RepresentationModelSpecialFindNode.label: Representation Model Special Find
RepresentationModelSpecialFindNode.description: 3D representation of a Special Find — e.g. a scanned capital repositioned according to an anastylosis hypothesis. Linked via crm:P138_represents to a SpecialFindUnit / VirtualSpecialFind. Specialization of em:RepresentationModel.
