mapping.alternative: D1 Digital Object + P138 to SpecialFindUnit / VirtualSpecialFind
mapping.rationale: Subclass of em:RepresentationModel; target type (special find) is enforced structurally.

SemanticShapeNode.label: Semantic Shape
SemanticShapeNode.description: 3D proxy geometry (convex shapes or spheres) representing the spatial extent of a node. Used as a semantic proxy distinct from a full RepresentationModel: lighter weight, intended for spatial indexing and rough containment, not for visual rendering. Linked via crm:P138_represents to any Node.

mapping.alternative: SP5 Geometric Place Expression + E36 Visual Item (legacy)
mapping.rationale: PROVVISORIO (2026-09-21) — crmgeo:SP6_Declarative_Place è il candidato migliore, decisione rinviata da E.D. REPAIR: crmgeo:SP5_Geometric_Place_Expression is NOT declared in the document served at http://www.cidoc-crm.org/extensions/crmgeo/ — the namespace this datamodel emits — which carries CRMgeo 2.0 (draft) declaring SP1,2,3,4,6,7,10,11,12,13,14,15; SP5 survives only inside the scope note of SP6. (It IS declared in the CRMgeo 1.2 release, but under the FORTH namespace http://www.ics.forth.gr/isl/CRMgeo/, which is not the one written here.) crm:E73_Information_Object is the safe move that commits to nothing. The argument below is the one to re-read when the decision is taken: SP5 (CRMgeo) is the canonical class for geometric expressions of places — exactly what a proxy convex/sphere is. The legacy 'E36 Visual Item' was too generic (E36 is the appearance of any object). v1.6.0 promotes SP5 to primary.

SemanticShapeNode.scope_note: SINCE v1.6.2 THE SEMANTIC SHAPE IS A PAYLOAD, not a standalone proxy. The proxy of a unit — its geometry-without-material — is a PropertyNode of qualia type 'geometry' (em_qualia_types.json, spatial), and the SemanticShape is what that property POINTS AT through has_semantic_shape: the numbers (convex hulls, spheres) or the .glb in its url. The reason is paradata: a lone shape hanging off a unit cannot say where it came from, so 'the proxy of US101' could not be traced to a measurement, a photograph or a reprojection; as the payload of a property it inherits the extractor/combiner chain, and ONE proxy can be synthesised from several sources. The node itself is unchanged — same fields, same CIDOC mapping, same file — what changed is who points at it. type_options: 'proxy' now names the ROLE OF THE CARRIER (this shape is the geometry of something) and no longer implies a standalone proxy node; 'generic' is any other spatial annotation. Consumers that read the proxy as a lone SemanticShape (EM-blender-tools, Heriverse) must follow the property instead — a declared breaking change with a one-shot legacy migration.

AnnotationRegionNode.label: Annotation Region
AnnotationRegionNode.description: The PLACE A READING LOOKED AT, in the source it read (geometry_kind): a region of one image or page in NORMALISED image coordinates [0,1] (region2d, the default: shape_kind rect|polygon, rect [x,y,w,h] or points [[x,y], ...], page index), a passage of a text (passage: start, end, text — character offsets plus the quoted words), or a point, a line or an open polyline on a 3D model (point|line|polyline), or a volume on it (volume: an annotation on the asset whose convex hulls and spheres are the SemanticShape it reaches with has_semantic_shape, node datamodel 1.6.16). For the 3D kinds the vertices ARE in the node (node datamodel 1.6.15): data.coords with crs and, for a line or a polyline, the length with its unit — up to coords.inline_max_vertices, above which they go to a .glb resource (has_linked_resource). Attached to what it is on (the image, the document, the model) with is_on_resource, read by an extractor with extracted_from, and the precise target of has_visual_reference from a PropertyNode.
AnnotationRegionNode.scope_note: USE for the place a reading looked at: a portion of a picture - 'this brick, in this photograph, on page 3' - a passage of a text, or a point / line / polyline on a 3D model. DO NOT USE for the geometry of a UNIT in the 3D space of the scene: that is its proxy, a SemanticShapeNode (crmgeo:SP5, a proxy hull or sphere expressing WHERE a thing is). They are separate classes because they answer different questions in different coordinate systems; one field set with a kind flag would force every reader to work out which meaning it was holding before it could use the numbers. DO NOT USE for a place either: a spatial grouping of units is LocationNodeGroup (E53 Place), which is about the world, not about an image of it. An AnnotationRegion makes no claim about where anything is - it says which part of which picture was looked at.
AnnotationRegionNode.rationale: A region of a visual item IS a visual item, hence crm:E36_Visual_Item, and its part-of relation to the whole image is P106i_forms_part_of (symbolic/informational mereology) - NOT P46i, which is physical containment between things and is also the drawing's nesting axis. Coordinates are normalised because a pixel region is only readable next to the resolution it was drawn at, and the same photograph is routinely re-exported at another size; normalised coordinates are a statement about the picture rather than about a file, and they express directly as a W3C Media Fragment. OPEN QUESTION (to confirm with Felicetti): the fine CIDOC modelling of the geometry itself - a selector literal (as here, aligned with the W3C Web Annotation model) versus a CRMgeo SP* geometric expression. The HOUSE of the node (E36 Visual Item) is decided; the selector is the interoperable form defensible today, and a refinement changes the projection of ONE field, not the class.

mapping.alternative: E36 Visual Item + crmgeo:SP* geometric expression (to confirm with Felicetti)
mapping.rationale: E36 is the appearance of a thing, which is exactly what a region of an image is a part of. The geometry travels as a SELECTOR literal (Media Fragment for a rect, SVG-style point list for a polygon) via em:hasSelector, so a consumer outside EM can act on it without reading this datamodel.

em_extension.rationale: A DISTINCT uri because E36 Visual Item is also the co-type the exporter puts on an image ResourceNode (has_visual_reference): without its own class the projection could not say whether a node was the picture or a region of it, which is the bijectivity the RDF round-trip depends on.

properties.name: P1_is_identified_by
properties.coords: geo:hasGeometry -> geo:Geometry at <region>/geometry, geo:asWKT '<CRS IRI> POINT Z (x y z)' | 'MULTIPOINT Z (...)' | 'LINESTRING Z (...)'^^geo:wktLiteral (GeoSPARQL 1.1); the CRS IRI is em:LocalSceneFrame for crs 'local', http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/<n> for 'EPSG:<n>'
properties.unit: P91_has_unit on the E54 -> QUDT unit IRI (m, cm, mm, km), else s3d:unit_<u>

shape_kinds.mask: PHASE 2 - declared, not implemented: a raster mask needs a payload (a PNG, an RLE) and a place to keep it, which is a resource-layer decision. The class REFUSES it rather than accepting it and storing nothing.

AnnotationRegionNode.coordinate_space: region2d: normalised image space, origin top-left, x and y in [0,1]; page is 0-based. passage: character offsets into the text as shown. point/line/polyline: the model's glTF frame (Y-up, scene-local, metres) — in data.coords, or in a .glb resource above coords.inline_max_vertices. volume: the same frame, in the SemanticShape it reaches.

geometry_kinds.region2d: DEFAULT, and every region written before 2026-10-06. On an image or one page: shape_kind + rect|points + page, in the node's data.
geometry_kinds.passage: On a text: start, end (0 <= start <= end, character offsets into the text as shown) and text (the quoted words) — W3C TextPositionSelector + TextQuoteSelector. Selector string: RFC 5147 'char=start,end'. In the node's data.
geometry_kinds.point: On a 3D model: one or more points. data.coords [[x, y, z], ...], vertex_count, crs. glTF (geometry_to_gltf): mode 0 POINTS.
geometry_kinds.line: On a 3D model: a measure, exactly 2 vertices. data.coords, vertex_count, length (computed from coords), unit, crs. glTF: mode 3 LINE_STRIP (mode 1 LINES read too).
geometry_kinds.polyline: On a 3D model: an articulated measure, an OPEN chain of >= 2 vertices. data.coords, vertex_count, length (sum of the segments), unit, crs. glTF: mode 3 LINE_STRIP.
geometry_kinds.volume: On a 3D model: a VOLUME that encloses a part of it — an annotation on the asset, not the proxy of a unit (ATON's semantic nodes with no EM node of the same name: «face», «cracks»). No vertices in the node: the convex hulls and spheres are a SemanticShapeNode the region reaches with has_semantic_shape (data.convexshapes flat [x,y,z, ...] per hull, data.spheres [x, y, z, r]; the model's glTF frame), the model is the target of is_on_resource. Made by geometry.aton.import_aton_scene; api.promote_region_to_proxy(region_id, unit_id) makes the shape the unit's proxy (US -> Property(geometry) -> shape) and removes the region, or keeps it as a trace (data.promoted_to) when something else points at it. glTF: the shape's TRIANGLES (geometry_to_gltf of the shape).

coords.field: data.coords = [[x, y, z], ...]: the vertices of a point, line or polyline IN THE NODE (E.D. 2026-09-30: geometry is divided by ORIGIN, not by shape — the sign of whoever argues is data of the node; what was acquired or processed is a file, a resource with its DTC stamp).
coords.frame: the frame of the model the reading is on — the frame the proxies' .glb are written in: glTF, Y-up, scene-local (net of the GeoPositionNode shift), metres. crs 'local'. Written verbatim, never converted.
coords.frame_iri_note: 1.6.18: the IRI that opens the geo:wktLiteral of coords when crs is 'local' (geometry/wkt.py crs_iri); 'EPSG:<n>' opens with http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/<n>, anything else with a minted s3d:crs_<slug>. The crs itself leaves as em:crs (properties.crs) on the E54 of the length, <region>/length, and nowhere else: a point has no length, and its frame is only in the literal.
coords.stitch: 1.6.16 · a polyline that comes back as glTF LINES pairs (Blender 5.x exports an edges-only mesh as mode 1, every inner vertex twice: 4 vertices -> 6) is stitched back into ONE ordered open chain by gltf_to_geometry: consecutive pairs that share a vertex within stitch_tolerance (metres, the coordinates' unit) are joined. Pairs that do not make a single open chain (two pieces, a branch, a closed loop) give a warning and the pieces, never an invented order. The kind of the reading is read from the glTF node's extras (em_reading_kind, where Blender writes an object's custom properties with export_extras) when the caller does not say it; geometry_to_gltf writes it there too, so Blender's importer makes it a custom property.
coords.above_threshold: more than inline_max_vertices vertices leave the node for a .glb: region -has_linked_resource-> ResourceNode(url readings/<region id>.glb, url_type 3d_model), with a warning that says so. The node keeps vertex_count, length, unit, crs. Read by nodes/annotation_region_node.inline_max_vertices(), never a constant in the code.
coords.gltf: Blender and EMStudio 3D speak glTF only; the conversion is s3Dgraphy's: geometry.gltf.geometry_to_gltf(node) -> bytes, gltf_to_geometry(bytes, kind) -> dict (POINTS, LINE_STRIP, and TRIANGLES for a SemanticShape's convex hulls).
coords.legacy: 2026-10-06 .. 2026-10-11 the vertices were readings/<region id>.glb, reached with has_semantic_shape -> SemanticShape(type generic, url). On opening from a file the glb is read into data.coords, the shape and its edge leave the graph; the file stays where it is, pointed at by nothing. Without the file (or without a folder) the old form stays and a warning says so.
coords.measure: api.measure(graph, region_id, project_root=None): vertex_count and length from data.coords; for a region whose vertices are in a .glb resource, the cached length, and with a project_root the file is re-read and compared.

AuthorNode.label: Author (human)
AuthorNode.description: Human author of one or more nodes. Identified by ORCID where possible. Python: AuthorNode (node_type='author'). The AI-assisted variant is AuthorAINode (subclass of AuthorNode). An isinstance check against AuthorNode matches both at the code level; the node_type discriminator and the em_extension.uri distinguish them semantically.

mapping.rationale: AuthorNode in Python is the canonical human-author class (node_type='author'). The em.ttl ontology declares em:Author as the abstract superclass with em:HumanAuthor / em:AIAuthor as siblings; the Python AuthorAINode inherits from AuthorNode purely for code reuse and isinstance() compatibility, not for OWL subsumption.

spatiotemporal.end: date of death (absolute_time_end): its label is «date of death» / «data di scomparsa», never a word for a thing that stops working
spatiotemporal.lane: has_first_epoch: the epoch of the study where the person begins to act in it, survive_in_epoch the others
spatiotemporal._ai_note: AuthorAINode reads the same fields as release and retirement of the model (em_qualia_types 1.6.9 owner_names)

AuthorAINode.label: AI Author
AuthorAINode.description: AI agent (model + prompt_reference) responsible for asserting or refining one or more nodes. Python: AuthorAINode (node_type='author_ai'), subclass of AuthorNode. Already referenced as target in connections_datamodel.json has_author edge. The Python class carries 'model' and 'prompt_reference' in node.data for reproducibility.

mapping.rationale: AI agents are formally PROV-O SoftwareAgents; CIDOC E39 Actor is the parent on the CRM side. Reproducibility metadata (model identifier, prompt_reference) lives in node.data and is EM-specific — no native CRM equivalent.

LicenseNode.label: License
LicenseNode.description: Represents the license under which a node (or the whole graph via GraphNode) is published. Identified by license_type (e.g. 'CC-BY-4.0') and url to the license text. Connected via has_license edge to Nodes or GraphNode.

mapping.rationale: License is naturally an E30 Right in CIDOC-CRM (subject of P104_is_subject_to); dcterms:LicenseDocument provides Dublin Core anchoring for FAIR metadata interoperability. Both parents are kept to satisfy both CRM and Dublin Core consumers.

EmbargoNode.label: Embargo
EmbargoNode.description: Represents a temporal embargo on access or distribution of a node, license, or whole graph. Carries embargo_start, embargo_end (optional, indefinite if absent), and reason. Connected via has_embargo edge to a Node, LicenseNode, or GraphNode.

mapping.rationale: An embargo is a Right (E30) that restricts access for a bounded time period (linked via P4_has_time-span to E52 Time-Span built from embargo_start and embargo_end). Sibling to LicenseNode but with temporal restriction semantics.

GraphNode.label: Graph
GraphNode.description: Represents the EM graph itself as a node, used as anchor for graph-wide metadata (author, license, embargo, default epoch, project-level provenance). Enables graph-level inheritance for metadata propagation: values declared on the GraphNode become defaults for all contained nodes unless overridden. Targeted by has_author, has_license, has_embargo edges to carry global defaults. In HDT-O terms (D7.1) an EM graph IS a Heritage Proposition Set (HC16) — a named graph carrying formal assertions about a heritage entity. Connectable via contains_proposition_set (HP33) to one or more HDTNode (HC2 Heritage Digital Twin) instances.

mapping.rationale: GraphNode is conceptually three things simultaneously: an information artifact (E73), a bundle of triples (prov:Bundle), and a Heritage Proposition Set (hdto:HC16 from D7.1). Multi-typing captures all three perspectives — a CRM-only reader sees E73, a PROV-O reader sees Bundle, an HDT-O reader sees HC16 attachable to HC2 HDTs.

HDTNode.label: Heritage Digital Twin
HDTNode.description: Represents an HC2 Heritage Digital Twin (HDT-O, ECHOES D7.1). An HDT is a named container that aggregates Heritage Proposition Sets (em:EMGraph instances) about a heritage entity (HC1). HDTs can be nested hierarchically via has_digital_twin_component (HP3 inverse) — e.g. Colosseo_HDT_overall has component Colosseo_HDT_Flavian. An EM graph attaches to an HDT via contains_proposition_set (HP33). The HDT is linked to its real-world heritage entity (HC1) via has_digital_twin (HP1).

mapping.rationale: HC2 is the canonical HDT-O class for a Heritage Digital Twin. Per D7.1 §4.1: aggregate of named graphs carrying formal propositions about an HC1 Heritage Entity. Multi-typed via HC14 / D1 so consumers that don't know HDT-O still see a CRMdig Digital Object.

hdto_nodes._section_note: HDT-O (ECHOES D7.1) layer node types — the HDTO VIEW. Gated out of the default stratigrapher palette (EMStudio palette-ui lists node types explicitly; these are omitted). Authored in HDT-aware tooling and projected to RDF. HC2 (HDTNode) and HC16 (GraphNode/em:EMGraph) are the pre-existing HDT-O-view members in container_nodes.

HeritageEntityNode.label: Heritage Entity
HeritageEntityNode.description: HC1 Heritage Entity (HDT-O, ECHOES D7.1): the real-world entity socially recognized as having cultural/historical/scientific value that an HC2 Heritage Digital Twin (HDTNode) is a digital twin of. Completes the canonical HDT-O chain HC1 -has_digital_twin(HP1)-> HC2 -contains_proposition_set(HP33)-> HC16 (em:EMGraph/GraphNode). HDT-O-view node: not shown in the stratigrapher palette (like HDTNode/GraphNode). HC3 Tangible / HC4 Intangible specializations are deferred.

mapping.rationale: HC1 is the canonical HDT-O class for the real-world heritage referent. Multi-typed via crm:E1 so consumers that don't know HDT-O still see a CRM Entity. Added in P1-C to give the has_digital_twin (HP1) edge a properly typed source (previously modelled as a generic Node/StratigraphicNode).

ProjectNode.label: Project
ProjectNode.description: HC13 Project (HDT-O, ECHOES D7.1): the coordinated activities of institutions/research groups producing heritage-related outcomes; the organizational context under which studies are carried out and under which HDTs are created and curated (HC11 maintenance is carried out under a project, HP20). Includes studies via crm:P9_consists_of (D7.1 defines no direct HC13->HC9 property). HDT-O-view node: not shown in the stratigrapher palette.

mapping.rationale: HC13 is the canonical HDT-O class for the research/organizational project. Multi-typed via crm:E7 Activity so consumers that don't know HDT-O still see a CRM Activity.

StudyNode.label: Study
StudyNode.description: HC9 Study (HDT-O, ECHOES D7.1): a scholarly activity (research/analysis/documentation, any domain) about a Heritage Entity (HC1), with a disciplinary focus, that produces documentary outputs contributing to an HDT. In EM a study heads a proposition set (HC16/em:EMGraph). Chain: Project -includes(crm:P9)-> Study -was_about(HP23)-> HeritageEntity ; Study -produced(HP25)-> GraphNode. HDT-O-view node: not shown in the stratigrapher palette.

mapping.alternative: hdto:HC9_Study ⊂ crm:E7_Activity; results in crm:E31 Document (HP25)
mapping.rationale: HC9 is the canonical HDT-O class for a scholarly study. Multi-typed via crm:E7 Activity. Per D7.1 a study is 'about' (HP23) an HC1 Heritage Entity and 'has created' (HP25) its documentary output — modelled here as the EM proposition set (HC16/em:EMGraph).

dtc_nodes._section_note: DTC (Data Transformation Chain) substrate profile — the ECHOES deliverable: the DIGITAL PROVENANCE around documents. TWO event step classes, both DISTINCT TYPES in the one DTC substrate: DTCProcessNode = GENESIS/transformation (crmdig:D7_Digital_Machine_Event) that produces documents (input Resources -> Process -> output Resources); DTCAcquisitionNode = ACQUISITION/ingestion (crmdig:D12_Data_Transfer_Event ⊂ D7) — how an asset ENTERS this study from an opaque external source (Tier 0: single-ring, acquisition --dtc_had_output--> Resource; source root recorded as literals). genesis != acquisition is a distinction of TYPE, never confused. Distinct from EM-paradata (interpretation ON a document = CRMinf/HC17). BOTH the INPUT and the OUTPUT are RESOURCES = the EM ResourceNode (E73/D1, the shared hinge a RepresentationModel/Document may reference), NOT dedicated classes: the process links to them via dtc_had_input / dtc_had_output (target ResourceNode); a Resource that participates carries data.dtc_kind + resource_type and projects crmdig:D1 + prov:Entity + P2(dtc_kind). The DTC graph = Resources connected by Process events (Process --dtc_had_input[prov:used]--> input Resource; Process --dtc_had_output[prov:generated]--> output Resource; output Resource --dtc_derived_from[prov:wasDerivedFrom]--> input Resource). Option A naming; CRMdig+PROV-O mapping in em_extension, no D-numbers in the UI. Gated OUT of the stratigrapher palette (like hdto_nodes). Per-kind vocabulary is DATA-DRIVEN + expandable in em_visual_rules.json -> dtc_kinds (via utils.get_dtc_kinds). EM commons (Author/License/Embargo/ResourceNode) reused, not duplicated. (ResourceNode -> ResourceNode rename is a future coordinated step.)

DTCProcessNode.label: DTC Process
DTCProcessNode.description: A DTC PROCESS step: the transformation/processing event that turns inputs into produced digital objects (data.dtc_kind from the `process` axis, e.g. transformation). Projected as a crmdig:D7_Digital_Machine_Event / prov:Activity; its inputs and outputs are the dtc_had_input (prov:used) and dtc_had_output (prov:generated) edges.

mapping.rationale: A digital processing step is a crmdig:D7 Digital Machine Event. Multi-typed prov:Activity so the PROV-O used/generated pattern applies directly.

technique.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): the free word of whoever did the gesture, beside the controlled dtc_kind. Leaves for RDF and comes back (it was lost by the round trip, measured on San Pietro).

parameters.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): how the technique was applied, a dict; ONE rdf:JSON literal, because the stamp format owns its shape.

software.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): the list of software of the step, each {name, version, commit?}; ONE rdf:JSON literal. data.tool is read back from its first entry, as declare_derivation writes it.

DTCAcquisitionNode.label: DTC Acquisition
DTCAcquisitionNode.description: A DTC ACQUISITION step: the digital event by which an asset ENTERS this study from an (opaque, Tier-0) external source — a data-transfer / ingestion event, DISTINCT from the genesis DTCProcessNode. Projected as crmdig:D12_Data_Transfer_Event (a subclass of D7_Digital_Machine_Event, ⊂ prov:Activity): 'events that transfer a digital object from one digital carrier to another; normally the digital object remains the same' — the object arrives opaque, no genesis is asserted. Tier 0: single-ring chain — the acquisition event --dtc_had_output[prov:generated]--> the acquired Resource (ResourceNode); the upstream root is an opaque external entity recorded as literals on data (repo/record/agent/retrieved_at/rights), not a genesis sub-graph. data.dtc_kind from the `acquisition` axis (two families since 1.6.22 — capture: photo / laserscanner / topographic / gnss_survey / field_drawing / recording_sheet; retrieval: download / local_import / uri_reference / ingest). Keeps genesis != acquisition as distinct TYPES inside the one DTC substrate.

mapping.alternative: crmdig:D12_Data_Transfer_Event (⊂ crmdig:D7_Digital_Machine_Event ⊂ prov:Activity) — dual CRMdig + PROV-O
mapping.rationale: An acquisition/ingestion is the transfer of a digital object from the source carrier to ours (D12), a more specific and DISTINCT class from the genesis D7 process event. Multi-typed prov:Activity so the PROV-O used/generated pattern applies (prov:generated the acquired Resource).
mapping.by_kind: 1.6.14 · D12 is the class of a RETRIEVAL. A CAPTURE makes the object rather than transferring it, and its kind declares the class the node takes instead (em_visual_rules 1.6.24, dtc_kinds.acquisition.<kind>.mapping): photo / laserscanner → crmdig:D2_Digitization_Process; topographic / gnss_survey → crmdig:D11_Digital_Measurement_Event; field_drawing / recording_sheet → crm:E65_Creation. The rule is data, read by the RDF exporter and importer alike.

technique.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): the free word of whoever did the gesture, beside the controlled dtc_kind. Leaves for RDF and comes back (it was lost by the round trip, measured on San Pietro).

parameters.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): how the technique was applied, a dict; ONE rdf:JSON literal, because the stamp format owns its shape.

software.note: 1.6.23 (dev29): the list of software of the step, each {name, version, commit?}; ONE rdf:JSON literal. data.tool is read back from its first entry, as declare_derivation writes it.

retrieved_from.note: 1.6.24 (dev30, decided by E.D. 2 Oct 2026, D1): WHERE A RETRIEVED OBJECT CAME FROM — the DOI (as https://doi.org/…) or the URL a Download was made from; the stamp's how.acquisition.retrieved_from. Not from[]: from[] names parents with an identity (a digest), and an origin has none. On the node it is one of the event's facts, data.retrieved_from (bucket_acquisition's metadata) or data.acquisition.retrieved_from (an absorbed stamp): dtc.ingest.acquisition_origin reads both. OPTIONAL in the format — validate warns «download without origin» for a dtc_kind download that does not say it, never an error, so an old stamp stays readable; EMStudio's composer requires it for a Download and fills it when it can be read. Leaves as em:retrievedFrom (xsd:anyURI for a URL) and comes back as data.retrieved_from.

DTCDeviceNode.label: DTC Device
DTCDeviceNode.description: The APPARATUS a DTC step happened on — camera, sensor, drone, computer, scanner, total station, GNSS receiver. Projected as crmdig:D8_Digital_Device and attached to the EVENT by dtc_happened_on_device (crmdig:L12_happened_on_device), never to the input or the output: the three dtc_kinds flow axes are what went in, what happened and what came out, and a device is what it happened ON. Until 2026-09-16 it was a STRING inside how.acquisition, and a string cannot be asked «what did this machine produce» or «that lens was distorted, which models are affected». NOT a DTCNode: a DTC node is a STEP (an event in the chain) and a device is a thing in the world — it has no inputs, no outputs, and a provenance walk has no business entering it; subclassing would have put it in the chain by inheritance and set the class hierarchy arguing with dtc_role. data.dtc_kind comes from the `device` axis of dtc_kinds (em_visual_rules.json), so adding an apparatus is a JSON entry plus a sign. THE ID IS DERIVED FROM THE DESCRIPTOR (make | model | serial) by uuid5 — the same mechanism bucket_acquisition uses for a campaign name, but WITHOUT the graph_id in the key, because a campaign is an event of one study while the same camera in two studies is one camera. WHAT THAT COSTS, DECLARED: without a serial number two identical bodies derive the same id and MERGE, and the graph then cannot say which body took a given file. data.distinguishes records which happened ('serial' = one body, 'make+model' = a model). A declared merge is better than an invented distinction: salting the id with a graph or a timestamp would make two records of the SAME camera look like two cameras, and that failure is silent. Gated out of the stratigrapher palette, like every DTC node.

mapping.rationale: crmdig:D8_Digital_Device (CRMdig 5.0) is the class L12_happened_on_device ranges over, so the node and the edge come from one place in one ontology. NO PROV-O co-typing: prov:Agent means 'a thing that bears some form of responsibility for an activity' and a camera bears none, while prov:Entity is what dtc_had_input's targets already are — typing a device as one would put the apparatus among the files. A PROV-only reader sees the step and its files, and no false statement about an agent.

georeferencing_nodes._section_note: GEOREFERENCING — how a produced model got INTO the world, as two distinct things that fail differently: GCPSetNode = the CONTROL (evidence: which point was seen on which photograph at which pixel, and where it is in the world, in which CRS, with what uncertainty) — it can exist before any model and survives being reused by a second reconstruction; RegistrationTransformNode = the SOLUTION (the 7-parameter similarity the bundle adjustment settled on, with its RMS/residuals) — it is what the model is placed by and what gets REPLACED when better coordinates arrive, the old one staying in the graph because moving a model is provenance. The TWO MODES of the photogrammetry design are the SHAPE of the graph, not a flag: absolute = a transform with a crs that has_gcp_set points at; local = a transform with a scale and crs=null (scaled and oriented in a site frame, honestly NOT georeferenced); no transform at all = nobody placed it. Distinct from GeoPositionNode (where a STUDY/site is) and from SemanticShapeNode (3D geometry of a unit): this section is about the REGISTRATION ACT's evidence and result. Attached to the produced Resource, so the DTC genesis (crmdig:D7, dtc_had_input/dtc_had_output) is not duplicated here. Gated OUT of the stratigrapher palette, like dtc_nodes and hdto_nodes. Added 2026-08-29 with the photogrammetry processing connector; ADDITIVE — no existing family changed.

GCPSetNode.label: Ground control points
GCPSetNode.description: The set of ground control points a registration was (or will be) solved from. data.points is a list of {id, world:[x,y,z], observations:[{image, pixel:[x,y]}], uncertainty?}; data.crs names the frame the world coordinates are in (null = a site-local grid, which is a different statement from absent). Minimum 3 observed non-collinear points for a similarity to be determined — reported by `solvable`, enforced by the runner, never at construction (a set being assembled in the field is legitimately incomplete). 1.6.24 (dev30, decided by E.D. 2 Oct 2026, D7): data.control says WHAT the points are — ground_control_points (default, not written) or camera_positions: the GPS positions of the cameras themselves, each point {id, world, image, uncertainty?} with no pixel observation (the camera is where the photograph was taken from, not something seen in it), solvable with three; data.accuracy_m is the accuracy the project records for the cameras. A chunk referenced only by its cameras' GPS is placed absolute with such a set, and validate warns «georeferenced only by camera GPS»: absolute without the control said would claim more than the data.

mapping.rationale: A control set is an INFORMATION OBJECT: a documented list of measured places and where each was observed. It is not itself a Place (crm:E53) nor a Measurement (crmsci:S21) — it CARRIES both. The individual observations stay payload literals in v1 and the explicit refinement is declared, not implied: each point would explode into an crmsci:S21_Measurement of an crm:E53_Place observed on a crmdig:D1 photograph. Doing that now would create three nodes per control point in a graph nobody yet reads that way.

em_extension.rationale: Named in the EM extension because 'the set of control points behind this registration' is the unit archaeologists actually hand each other, and CIDOC has no class for it above E73.

RegistrationTransformNode.label: Registration transform
RegistrationTransformNode.description: The 7-parameter similarity (rotation 3x3 row-major, translation [x,y,z], positive scale) that places a produced model, with data.rms and data.residuals — the error bar, stored beside the claim rather than in a log nobody keeps. data.crs is the frame the model lands IN; null means a site-local frame (mode 'local'), which is NOT the same sentence as an absent transform. Re-registration is a NEW node produced by a NEW crmdig:D7; the superseded one is never edited.

mapping.rationale: The transform is an information object that DESCRIBES a mapping between two spatial reference systems (crmgeo:SP4_Spatial_Coordinate_Reference_System). CIDOC/CRMgeo models coordinate systems and geometric expressions but has no class for the parameterised map between two of them, so E73 is the honest superclass and the specificity lives in em:RegistrationTransform. It is deliberately NOT an event: the ACT of registering is the crmdig:D7 that produced this object.

em_extension.rationale: Proposed rather than asserted: the natural CRM-native alternative is to leave the parameters as literals on the D7 event, which loses the ability to point at 'the placement' as a thing that gets superseded — and superseding it is the whole reason mode (b) exists.

narrative_nodes._section_note: EM Narrative (DP-79, draft). A narrative is the story told OVER a graph: chapters anchored to the graph's lanes (epochs, activities), each carrying prose and embeds. It is a first-class node so it can be queried ('which narratives cite this US', 'which rest on a withdrawn source'), versioned and carried through the DTC. Chapters and blocks are NOT nodes: they are ordered structures inside node.data — EM has no ordered-edge primitive, and a chapter has no existence apart from its narrative. An embed holds only the stable id of the resource it shows, never a copy of it, so a narrative always says what the graph currently says.

NarrativeNode.label: Narrative
NarrativeNode.description: A narrative over the EM graph: an ordered sequence of chapters, each anchored to a lane (epoch, activity, area) or standing outside the stratigraphy (introduction, geographic placement), and each composed of prose blocks and embed blocks. An embed references an EM resource by its stable id and declares a view_type (matrix, scene3d, us, rm, document, source, paradata, map, timeline, table, un_scene; 'epoch3d' is the retired spelling of 'scene3d' and is still accepted on read) saying how it should be shown. Metadata follows the existing conventions: author / license / embargo (DP-32), lang (DP-63), version, and template_id recording which scaffolder produced the first draft.
NarrativeNode.scope_note: Authored on the property graph (em.json) and PROJECTED to RDF — never triple-first. The narrative is a distinct thing from its renderings: one NarrativeNode can drive a live web viewer, a LaTeX print, a docx snapshot or a Jupyter notebook, and adding a target means adding a resolver, not re-authoring. Chapters marked canonical are the ones the author has settled: a template regeneration must leave them untouched. NOT a substitute for the paradata chain — a narrative CITES evidence (embed view_type=paradata), it does not restate it.

mapping.alternative: E33 Linguistic Object + E73 Information Object
mapping.rationale: E33 is the CIDOC class for a text: the narrative IS linguistic content about the heritage entity. It is multi-typed E73 because it is also an identifiable information object that can be versioned, licensed and embargoed like the graph itself (GraphNode uses E73 for the same reason). The embeds are not content: they are references, projected as P67_refers_to towards the referenced node IRIs, which is what makes 'which narratives cite this US' answerable in SPARQL without parsing prose.

valid_view_types.matrix: The matrix, or a slice of one epoch
valid_view_types.scene3d: A 3D scene (Heriverse / ATON). The embed points at the graph's published scene id or at a RepresentationModel — the scene is a GRAPH-level thing, not an epoch's: has_linked_resource does not admit an EpochNode as source, so an epoch has no EM-legal way to hold geometry.
valid_view_types.us: A stratigraphic unit with its certainty qualia
valid_view_types.source: A source together with its criticism
valid_view_types.paradata: The evidence chain: source -> extractor -> property
valid_view_types.timeline: A temporal axis of the narrated epochs

TranslationNode.label: Translation
TranslationNode.description: ONE TRANSLATION of one text field of one node (E.D. 2026-10-01, «Le traduzioni»). The ORIGINAL stays a string in its own field, in the language it was written in — data.lang on the node says which, else the study's working language — and a translation never overwrites it: the original is testimony. Each translation is a node of its own, reached from the translated node by has_translation (reverse is_translation_of). Fields in data: lang (the language of ARRIVAL, BCP 47 — the same key as every node's data.lang, so its own text takes its tag by the ordinary cascade); from_lang (the language of DEPARTURE, the original's WHEN it was translated: written, because the original can change); field (the translated field in the CRDT's vocabulary: description, or data.<key> — a PropertyNode's value is data.value; name is never translated, names are invariant identities); text; method (manual | ai | edition); source_digest ('sha256:<hex>' of the original text translated, NFC + UTF-8: when the original changes the digests differ and the translation is «da riallineare», which no signature clears); review_requested (true when the translator asks for a review, «da rivedere»). WHO translated is has_author (an AuthorNode); WHEN is the editorial stamp created_at. An AI translation carries data.ai_assisted and stays among the warnings until a person verifies it (data.validated_by / validated_at, the same two fields that close a requested review: ai_validation.verify). A translation from a published EDITION reaches the DocumentNode of that edition with extracted_from: a published translation is a source, Vitruvius read through a translator is an interpretation.

mapping.rationale: crm:E33_Linguistic_Object is CIDOC's class for a text in a natural language, and a translation is one; CIDOC also has the relation, P73_has_translation (E33 → E33), carried by the has_translation edge, so no em: class is minted: the term exists. The narrative is also an E33 (em:Narrative ⊂ E33); a translation is typed by the CIDOC class alone, and the RDF importer tells the two apart because E33 is only a SUPERCLASS for the narrative. The translation's provenance leaves as PROV-O on the node itself: prov:wasDerivedFrom → the translated node, prov:wasAttributedTo → its author (has_author).

TranslationNode.properties_note: 1.6.20: the RDF projection of each field (rdf_exporter._serialize_translation). text leaves as crm:P190_has_symbolic_content tagged with lang, which is also written as crm:P72_has_language; the four em: terms (em.ttl 1.6.10) say what CIDOC does not — which field of the original, from which language, how, of which text; review_requested is written only when true. The node also leaves prov:wasDerivedFrom → the translated node, the PROV reading of has_translation (crm:P73), which the importer reads as its companion and never as an edge. On the TRANSLATED node, each aligned translation adds one literal on the predicate of its field (dcterms:description, or crm:P90_has_value for a PropertyNode's data.value) with its own tag; a translation to realign adds none.

UnknownNode.label: Unknown node
UnknownNode.description: Fallback node for unrecognized types. This type of node should not normally appear in the system but serves exclusively to handle anomalies in the data.

em_extension.rationale: Distinct from em:Node: 'the source could not type this' is a different statement from 'this is the base class', and a consumer that wants to find the anomalies must be able to ask for them. Both remain E1 for CRM-only readers.
